75.s:
nārada uvāca
kailāsaśikharaṃ gatvā gautamo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
kiṃ cakāra tapo vāpi kāṃ cakre stutim uttamām //
75.d:
नारद उवाच
कैलासशिखरं गत्वा गौतमो भगवान् ऋषिः
किं चकार तपो वापि कां चक्रे स्तुतिम् उत्तमाम् ॥
75.m: Nārada said: / Having gone to the summit of Kailāsa, what asceticism did the venerable ṛṣi / Gautama perform, or what excellent hymn of praise did he recite?

75.s:
brahmovāca
giriṃ gatvā tato vatsa vācaṃ saṃyamya gautamaḥ
āstīrya sa kuśān prājñaḥ kailāse parvatottame //
75.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गिरिं गत्वा ततो वत्स वाचं संयम्य गौतमः
आस्तीर्य स कुशान् प्राज्ञः कैलासे पर्वतोत्तमे ॥
75.m: Brahmā said: / Having gone to the mountain, my child, Gautama, restraining his speech, / the wise one, having strewn kuśa grass on Kailāsa, the excellent mountain,

75.s:
upaviśya śucir bhūtvā stotraṃ cedaṃ tato jagau
apatat puṣpavṛṣṭiś ca stūyamāne maheśvare //
75.d:
उपविश्य शुचिर् भूत्वा स्तोत्रं चेदं ततो जगौ
अपतत् पुष्पवृष्टिश् च स्तूयमाने महेश्वरे ॥
75.m: and sat down, having become purified, then sang this hymn of praise; / and a shower of flowers fell while Maheśvara was being praised.

75.s:
gautama uvāca
bhogārthināṃ bhogam abhīpsitaṃ ca
dātuṃ mahānty aṣṭavapūṃṣi dhatte
somo janānāṃ guṇavanti nityaṃ
devaṃ mahādevam iti stuvanti
75.d:
गौतम उवाच
भोगार्थिनां भोगम् अभीप्सितं च
दातुं महान्त्य् अष्टवपूंषि धत्ते
सोमो जनानां गुणवन्ति नित्यं
देवं महादेवम् इति स्तुवन्ति
75.m: Gautama said: / In order to grant desired enjoyment to those who seek enjoyment, / Soma constantly assumes eight great bodies endowed with qualities for the sake of living beings; / they praise this god as Mahādeva.

75.s:
kartuṃ svakīyair viṣayaiḥ sukhāni
bhartuṃ samastaṃ sacarācaraṃ ca
saṃpattaye hy asya vivṛddhaye ca
mahīmayaṃ rūpam itīśvarasya
75.d:
कर्तुं स्वकीयैर् विषयैः सुखानि
भर्तुं समस्तं सचराचरं च
संपत्तये ह्य् अस्य विवृद्धये च
महीमयं रूपम् इतीश्वरस्य
75.m: To produce pleasures through its own objects, / to sustain all that moves and does not move, / and for its prosperity and growth, / the Lord's form consists of the earth.

75.s:
sṛṣṭeḥ sthiteḥ saṃharaṇāya bhūmer
ādhāram ādhātum apāṃ svarūpam
bheje śivaḥ śāntatanur janānāṃ
sukhāya dharmāya jagat pratiṣṭhitam
75.d:
सृष्टेः स्थितेः संहरणाय भूमेर्
आधारम् आधातुम् अपां स्वरूपम्
भेजे शिवः शान्ततनुर् जनानां
सुखाय धर्माय जगत् प्रतिष्ठितम्
75.m: For the creation, preservation, and destruction of the earth, / and to provide a foundation, Śiva, whose body is tranquil, / assumed the nature of water for the happiness of people and for dharma, [upon which] the world is established.

75.s:
kālavyavasthām amṛtasravaṃ ca
jīvasthitiṃ sṛṣṭim atho vināśanam
mudaṃ prajānāṃ sukham unnatiṃ ca
cakre 'rkacandrāgnimayaṃ śarīram
75.d:
कालव्यवस्थाम् अमृतस्रवं च
जीवस्थितिं सृष्टिम् अथो विनाशनम्
मुदं प्रजानां सुखम् उन्नतिं च
चक्रे ऽर्कचन्द्राग्निमयं शरीरम्
75.m: For the division of time and the flowing of nectar, / the sustenance of life, creation, and destruction, / the joy of creatures, their happiness, and their elevation, / he made a body composed of the sun, the moon, and fire.

75.s:
vṛddhiṃ gatiṃ śaktim athākṣarāṇi
jīvavyavasthāṃ mudam apy anekām
sraṣṭuṃ kṛtaṃ vāyur itīśarūpaṃ
tvaṃ vetsi nūnaṃ bhagavan bhavantam
75.d:
वृद्धिं गतिं शक्तिम् अथाक्षराणि
जीवव्यवस्थां मुदम् अप्य् अनेकाम्
स्रष्टुं कृतं वायुर् इतीशरूपं
त्वं वेत्सि नूनं भगवन् भवन्तम्
75.m: To create growth, movement, power, letters, / the maintenance of living beings, and manifold joy, / the form of the Lord was made as wind; / truly, O Lord, you know yourself.

75.s:
bhedair vinā naiva kṛtir na dharmo
nātmīyam anyan na diśo 'ntarikṣam
dyāvāpṛthivyau na ca bhuktimuktī
tasmād idaṃ vyomavapus taveśa
75.d:
भेदैर् विना नैव कृतिर् न धर्मो
नात्मीयम् अन्यन् न दिशो ऽन्तरिक्षम्
द्यावापृथिव्यौ न च भुक्तिमुक्ती
तस्माद् इदं व्योमवपुस् तवेश
75.m: Without divisions, there is no action, nor dharma, / nor anything of one's own, nor the directions, nor the atmosphere, / nor heaven and earth, nor worldly enjoyment and liberation; / therefore this ether-body is yours, O Lord.

75.s:
dharmaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ vyavasya
ṛksāmaśāstrāṇi yajuś ca śākhāḥ
loke ca gāthāḥ smṛtayaḥ purāṇam
ityādiśabdātmakatām upaiti
75.d:
धर्मं व्यवस्थापयितुं व्यवस्य
ऋक्सामशास्त्राणि यजुश् च शाखाः
लोके च गाथाः स्मृतयः पुराणम्
इत्यादिशब्दात्मकताम् उपैति
75.m:
Having resolved to establish dharma,
he assumes the nature of sound as the Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajur branches,
the treatises, the popular songs in the world,
the Smṛtis, the Purāṇa, and so forth.

75.s:
yaṣṭā kratur yāny api sādhanāni
ṛtvikpradeśaṃ phaladeśakālāḥ
tvam eva śaṃbho paramārthatattvaṃ
vadanti yajñāṅgamayaṃ vapus te
75.d:
यष्टा क्रतुर् यान्य् अपि साधनानि
ऋत्विक्प्रदेशं फलदेशकालाः
त्वम् एव शंभो परमार्थतत्त्वं
वदन्ति यज्ञाङ्गमयं वपुस् ते
75.m:
The sacrificer, the rite, and whatever implements,
the sacrificial priest, the place, the times and fruits [of rites]—
you alone, O Śambhu, are the highest reality;
they declare that your body consists of the constituents of sacrifice.

75.s:
kartā pradātā pratibhūḥ pradānaṃ
sarvajñasākṣī puruṣaḥ paraś ca
pratyātmabhūtaḥ paramārtharūpas
tvam eva sarvaṃ kim u vāgvilāsaiḥ
75.d:
कर्ता प्रदाता प्रतिभूः प्रदानं
सर्वज्ञसाक्षी पुरुषः परश् च
प्रत्यात्मभूतः परमार्थरूपस्
त्वम् एव सर्वं किम् उ वाग्विलासैः
75.m:
The agent, the bestower, the guarantor, the gift,
the omniscient witness, and the supreme puruṣa,
the inner self, possessing the form of ultimate truth,
you alone are everything; what need is there of flourishes of speech?

75.s:
na vedaśāstrair gurubhiḥ pradiṣṭo
na nāsi buddhyādibhir apradhṛṣyaḥ
ajo 'prameyaḥ śivaśabdavācyas
tvam asti satyaṃ bhagavan namas te
75.d:
न वेदशास्त्रैर् गुरुभिः प्रदिष्टो
न नासि बुद्ध्यादिभिर् अप्रधृष्यः
अजो ऽप्रमेयः शिवशब्दवाच्यस्
त्वम् अस्ति सत्यं भगवन् नमस् ते
75.m:
You are not taught by the Vedic scriptures or teachers,
nor are you not invincible to the intellect and other faculties;
unborn, immeasurable, denoted by the word Śiva,
you truly exist, O Lord, reverence to you!

75.s:
ātmaikatāṃ svaprakṛtiṃ kadācid
aikṣac chivaḥ saṃpad iyaṃ mameti
pṛthak tadaivābhavad apratarkya
acintyaprabhāvo bahuviśvamūrtiḥ
75.d:
आत्मैकतां स्वप्रकृतिं कदाचिद्
ऐक्षच् छिवः संपद् इयं ममेति
पृथक् तदैवाभवद् अप्रतर्क्य
अचिन्त्यप्रभावो बहुविश्वमूर्तिः
75.m:
Once, Śiva looked upon the oneness of the Self, his own Prakṛti, thinking:
‘This is my abundance!’
Immediately then, inconceivable and of unimaginable majesty,
he became distinct, having many cosmic forms.

75.s:
bhāve 'bhivṛddhā ca bhave bhave ca
svakāraṇaṃ kāraṇam āsthitā ca
nityā śivā sarvasulakṣaṇā vā
vilakṣaṇā viśvakarasya śaktiḥ
75.d:
भावे ऽभिवृद्धा च भवे भवे च
स्वकारणं कारणम् आस्थिता च
नित्या शिवा सर्वसुलक्षणा वा
विलक्षणा विश्वकरस्य शक्तिः
75.m:
Grown in existence, and in every birth and being,
she resides in her own cause, the primal cause;
eternal, auspicious, possessing every auspicious mark,
or beyond all marks: she is the power of the cosmic creator.

75.s:
utpādanaṃ saṃsthitir annavṛddhi
layāḥ satāṃ yatra sanātanās te
ekaiva mūrtir na samasti kiṃcid
asādhyam asyā dayitā harasya
75.d:
उत्पादनं संस्थितिर् अन्नवृद्धि
लयाः सतां यत्र सनातनास् ते
एकैव मूर्तिर् न समस्ति किंचिद्
असाध्यम् अस्या दयिता हरस्य
75.m:
Generation, preservation, increase of sustenance,
and dissolutions, where they are eternal for the good—
her form is single; nothing is impossible
for this beloved of Hara.

75.s:
yadartham annāni dhanāni jīvā
yacchanti kurvanti tapāṃsi dharmān
sāpīyam ambā jagato janitrī
priyā tu somasya mahāsukīrtiḥ
75.d:
यदर्थम् अन्नानि धनानि जीवा
यच्छन्ति कुर्वन्ति तपांसि धर्मान्
सापीयम् अम्बा जगतो जनित्री
प्रिया तु सोमस्य महासुकीर्तिः
75.m:
For whose sake living beings give food and wealth,
and perform austerities and virtuous deeds—
she, this mother, the creatress of the universe,
is the beloved of the Moon-crested One, of great and glorious fame.

75.s:
yad īkṣitaṃ kāṅkṣati vāsavo 'pi
yannāmato maṅgalam āpnuyāc ca
yā vyāpya viśvaṃ vimalīkaroti
somā sadā somasamānarūpā
75.d:
यद् ईक्षितं काङ्क्षति वासवो ऽपि
यन्नामतो मङ्गलम् आप्नुयाच् च
या व्याप्य विश्वं विमलीकरोति
सोमा सदा सोमसमानरूपा
75.m:
Whose glance even Indra desires,
from whose name one attains auspiciousness,
who pervades and purifies the universe,
accompanied by the Moon, ever resembling the Moon in form.

75.s:
brahmādijīvasya carācarasya
buddhyakṣicaitanyamanaḥsukhāni
yasyāḥ prasādāt phalavanti nityaṃ
vāgīśvarī lokaguroḥ suramyā
75.d:
ब्रह्मादिजीवस्य चराचरस्य
बुद्ध्यक्षिचैतन्यमनःसुखानि
यस्याः प्रसादात् फलवन्ति नित्यं
वागीश्वरी लोकगुरोः सुरम्या
75.m:
Of all moving and unmoving beings, beginning with Brahmā,
the delights of intellect, vision, consciousness, and mind
always bear fruit through her grace;
she is the goddess of speech, the exceedingly beautiful consort of the teacher of the worlds.

75.s:
caturmukhasyāpi mano malīnaṃ
kim anyajantor iti cintya mātā
gaṅgāvatāraṃ vividhair upāyaiḥ
sarvaṃ jagat pāvayituṃ cakāra
75.d:
चतुर्मुखस्यापि मनो मलीनं
किम् अन्यजन्तोर् इति चिन्त्य माता
गङ्गावतारं विविधैर् उपायैः
सर्वं जगत् पावयितुं चकार
75.m:
Reflecting: ‘Even the mind of the Four-faced One is sullied,
what then of other creatures?’, the Mother,
in order to purify the entire universe,
brought about the descent of the Gaṅgā by various means.

75.s:
śrutīḥ samālakṣya haraprabhutvaṃ
viśvasya lokaḥ sakalaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ
kṛtvā ca dharmān bubhuje ca bhogān
vibhūtir eṣā tu sadāśivasya
75.d:
श्रुतीः समालक्ष्य हरप्रभुत्वं
विश्वस्य लोकः सकलैः प्रमाणैः
कृत्वा च धर्मान् बुभुजे च भोगान्
विभूतिर् एषा तु सदाशिवस्य
75.m:
Seeing Hara’s lordship over the universe
through the Vedas by all means of valid cognition,
the world performed virtuous acts and enjoyed pleasures;
this indeed is the sovereign glory of Sadāśiva.

75.s:
kāryakriyākārakasādhanānāṃ
vedoditānām atha laukikānām
yat sādhyam utkṛṣṭatamaṃ priyaṃ ca
proktā ca sā siddhir anādikartuḥ
75.d:
कार्यक्रियाकारकसाधनानां
वेदोदितानाम् अथ लौकिकानाम्
यत् साध्यम् उत्कृष्टतमं प्रियं च
प्रोक्ता च सा सिद्धिर् अनादिकर्तुः
75.m:
Of effects, actions, agents, and instruments,
whether spoken of in the Vedas or worldly,
that which is to be accomplished, supreme and beloved—
that is declared to be the perfection of the beginningless creator.

75.s:
dhyātvā varaṃ brahma paraṃ pradhānaṃ
yat sārabhūtaṃ yad upāsitavyam
yat prāpya muktā na punar bhavanti
sadyogino muktir umāpatiḥ saḥ
75.d:
ध्यात्वा वरं ब्रह्म परं प्रधानं
यत् सारभूतं यद् उपासितव्यम्
यत् प्राप्य मुक्ता न पुनर् भवन्ति
सद्योगिनो मुक्तिर् उमापतिः सः
75.m:
Having meditated upon the excellent, supreme Brahman, the pradhāna,
that which is the essence, that which is to be worshiped,
having attained which the liberated do not return again—
that liberation for true yogins is the lord of Umā.

75.s:
yathā yathā śaṃbhur ameyamāyā
rūpāṇi dhatte jagato hitāya
tadyogayogyāni tathaiva dhatse
pativratātvaṃ tvayi mātar evam
75.d:
यथा यथा शंभुर् अमेयमाया
रूपाणि धत्ते जगतो हिताय
तद्योगयोग्यानि तथैव धत्से
पतिव्रतात्वं त्वयि मातर् एवम्
75.m:
In whatever ways Śambhu assumes forms
of immeasurable illusory power for the welfare of the world,
in those very ways you assume forms suited to union with him;
such is your wifely devotion, O Mother!

75.s:
brahmovāca
ity evaṃ stuvatas tasya purastād vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
umayā sahitaḥ śrīmān gaṇeśādigaṇair vṛtaḥ //
75.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् एवं स्तुवतस् तस्य पुरस्ताद् वृषभध्वजः
उमया सहितः श्रीमान् गणेशादिगणैर् वृतः ॥

75.s: sākṣād āgatya taṃ śaṃbhuḥ prasanno vākyam abravīt //
75.d: साक्षाद् आगत्य तं शंभुः प्रसन्नो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
75.m: Śambhu came in person and, being pleased, spoke these words:

75.s:
śiva uvāca
kiṃ te gautama dāsyāmi bhaktistotravrataiḥ śubhaiḥ
parituṣṭo 'smi yācasva devānām api duṣkaram //
75.d:
शिव उवाच
किं ते गौतम दास्यामि भक्तिस्तोत्रव्रतैः शुभैः
परितुष्टो ऽस्मि याचस्व देवानाम् अपि दुष्करम् ॥
75.m:
Śiva said:
What shall I grant you, O Gautama? By your auspicious vows of devotion and praises
I am well pleased; ask even for that which is difficult for the gods to attain!

75.s:
brahmovāca
iti śrutvā jaganmūrter vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
harṣabāṣpaparītāṅgo gautamaḥ paryacintayat //
75.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इति श्रुत्वा जगन्मूर्तेर् वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः
हर्षबाष्पपरीताङ्गो गौतमः पर्यचिन्तयत् ॥
75.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing the words of the one whose form is the world, Gautama, skilled in speech,
his limbs bathed in tears of joy, reflected:

75.s:
aho daivam aho dharmo hy aho vai viprapūjanam
aho lokagatiś citrā aho dhātar namo 'stu te //
75.d:
अहो दैवम् अहो धर्मो ह्य् अहो वै विप्रपूजनम्
अहो लोकगतिश् चित्रा अहो धातर् नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
75.m:
Ah, destiny! Ah, dharma! Ah, the worship of brāhmaṇas!
Ah, the wondrous course of the world! Ah, Creator, reverence to you!

75.s:
gautama uvāca
jaṭāsthitāṃ śubhāṃ gaṅgāṃ dehi me tridaśārcita
yadi tuṣṭo 'si deveśa trayīdhāma namo 'stu te //
75.d:
गौतम उवाच
जटास्थितां शुभां गङ्गां देहि मे त्रिदशार्चित
यदि तुष्टो ऽसि देवेश त्रयीधाम नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
75.m:
Gautama said:
Grant me the auspicious Gaṅgā residing in your matted hair, O you who are worshiped by the thirty gods!
If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, abode of the three Vedas, reverence to you!

75.s:
īśvara uvāca
trayāṇām upakārārthaṃ lokānāṃ yācitaṃ tvayā
ātmanas tūpakārāya tad yācasvākutobhayaḥ //
75.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
त्रयाणाम् उपकारार्थं लोकानां याचितं त्वया
आत्मनस् तूपकाराय तद् याचस्वाकुतोभयः ॥

75.s:
gautama uvāca
stotreṇānena ye bhaktās tvāṃ ca devīṃ stuvanti vai
sarvakāmasamṛddhāḥ syur etad dhi varayāmy aham //
75.d:
गौतम उवाच
स्तोत्रेणानेन ये भक्तास् त्वां च देवीं स्तुवन्ति वै
सर्वकामसमृद्धाः स्युर् एतद् धि वरयाम्य् अहम् ॥
75.m:
Gautama said:
May those devotees who praise you and the goddess with this hymn
be enriched with all desires; this indeed is the boon I choose!

75.s:
brahmovāca
evam astv iti deveśaḥ parituṣṭo 'bravīd vacaḥ
anyān api varān matto yācasva vigatajvaraḥ //
75.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् अस्त्व् इति देवेशः परितुष्टो ऽब्रवीद् वचः
अन्यान् अपि वरान् मत्तो याचस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
75.m:
Brahmā said:
The Lord of gods, well pleased, said: ‘So be it!’
‘Ask other boons from me as well, free from affliction!’

75.s: evam uktas tu harṣeṇa gautamaḥ prāha śaṃkaram //
75.d: एवम् उक्तस् तु हर्षेण गौतमः प्राह शंकरम् ॥
75.m: Having been spoken to thus, Gautama joyfully said to Śaṅkara:

75.s:
gautama uvāca
imāṃ devīṃ jaṭāsaṃsthāṃ pāvanīṃ lokapāvanīm
tava priyāṃ jagannātha utsṛja brahmaṇo girau //
75.d:
गौतम उवाच
इमां देवीं जटासंस्थां पावनीं लोकपावनीम्
तव प्रियां जगन्नाथ उत्सृज ब्रह्मणो गिरौ ॥
75.m:
Gautama said:
This goddess residing in your matted locks, the purifier, the purifier of the world,
your beloved, O Lord of the universe, release upon the mountain of Brahmā!

75.s:
sarvāsāṃ tīrthabhūtā tu yāvad gacchati sāgaram
brahmahatyādipāpāni manovākkāyikāni ca //
75.d:
सर्वासां तीर्थभूता तु यावद् गच्छति सागरम्
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि मनोवाक्कायिकानि च ॥
75.m:
Becoming the sacred tīrtha for all as long as she flows to the ocean,
may sins such as the killing of a brāhmaṇa, committed in mind, speech, and body,

75.s:
snānamātreṇa sarvāṇi vilayaṃ yāntu śaṃkara
candrasūryoparāge ca ayane viṣuve tathā //
75.d:
स्नानमात्रेण सर्वाणि विलयं यान्तु शंकर
चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे च अयने विषुवे तथा ॥
75.m:
all dissolve by merely bathing [in her], O Śaṅkara!
And during eclipses of the moon and sun, at the solstices and equinoxes,

75.s:
saṃkrāntau vaidhṛtau puṇyatīrtheṣv anyeṣu yat phalam
asyās tu smaraṇād eva tat puṇyaṃ jāyatāṃ hara //
75.d:
संक्रान्तौ वैधृतौ पुण्यतीर्थेष्व् अन्येषु यत् फलम्
अस्यास् तु स्मरणाद् एव तत् पुण्यं जायतां हर ॥
75.m:
at the saṃkrānti and the vaidhṛti, whatever fruit there is at other sacred tīrthas,
may that merit arise from merely remembering her, O Hara!

75.s:
ślāghyaṃ kṛte tapaḥ proktaṃ tretāyāṃ yajñakarma ca
dvāpare yajñadāne ca dānam eva kalau yuge //
75.d:
श्लाघ्यं कृते तपः प्रोक्तं त्रेतायां यज्ञकर्म च
द्वापरे यज्ञदाने च दानम् एव कलौ युगे ॥
75.m:
Austerity is declared praiseworthy in the Kṛta age, sacrificial rites in the Tretā,
sacrifice and charity in the Dvāpara, and charity alone in the Kali age.

75.s:
yugadharmāś ca ye sarve deśadharmās tathaiva ca
deśakālādisaṃyoge yo dharmo yatra śasyate //
75.d:
युगधर्माश् च ये सर्वे देशधर्मास् तथैव च
देशकालादिसंयोगे यो धर्मो यत्र शस्यते ॥
75.m:
Whatever are the duties of the ages, and likewise the customs of lands,
whatever duty is commended in a given conjunction of place, time, and circumstances,

75.s:
yad anyatra kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ snānadānādisaṃyamaiḥ
asyās tu smaraṇād eva tat puṇyaṃ jāyatāṃ hara //
75.d:
यद् अन्यत्र कृतं पुण्यं स्नानदानादिसंयमैः
अस्यास् तु स्मरणाद् एव तत् पुण्यं जायतां हर ॥
75.m:
and whatever merit is acquired elsewhere through baths, gifts, and self-restraint—
may that merit arise from merely remembering her, O Hara!

75.s:
yatra yatra tv iyaṃ yāti yāvat sāgaragāminī
tatra tatra tvayā bhāvyam eṣa cāstu varo varaḥ //
75.d:
यत्र यत्र त्व् इयं याति यावत् सागरगामिनी
तत्र तत्र त्वया भाव्यम् एष चास्तु वरो वरः ॥
75.m:
Wherever she flows until she reaches the ocean,
there you must be present; let this also be an excellent boon!

75.s:
yojanānāṃ tūpari tu daśa yāvac ca saṃkhyayā
tadantarapraviṣṭānāṃ mahāpātakinām api //
75.d:
योजनानां तूपरि तु दश यावच् च संख्यया
तदन्तरप्रविष्टानां महापातकिनाम् अपि ॥
75.m:
And up to a distance of ten yojanas,
for those who enter within that space, even great sinners,

75.s:
tat pitṝṇāṃ ca teṣāṃ ca snānāyāgacchatāṃ śiva
snāne cāpy antare mṛtyor muktibhājo bhavantu vai //
75.d:
तत् पितॄणां च तेषां च स्नानायागच्छतां शिव
स्नाने चाप्य् अन्तरे मृत्योर् मुक्तिभाजो भवन्तु वै ॥
75.m:
both for them and for their ancestors, when coming to bathe, O Śiva,
and if they die during the bath, may they indeed attain liberation!

75.s:
ekataḥ sarvatīrthāni svargamartyarasātale
eṣā tebhyo viśiṣṭā tu alaṃ śaṃbho namo 'stu te //
75.d:
एकतः सर्वतीर्थानि स्वर्गमर्त्यरसातले
एषा तेभ्यो विशिष्टा तु अलं शंभो नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
75.m:
On one side stand all the tīrthas in heaven, earth, and the netherworld;
she is superior to them. Enough, O Śambhu, reverence to you!

75.s:
brahmovāca
tad gautamavacaḥ śrutvā tathāstv ity abravīc chivaḥ
asyāḥ parataraṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati //
75.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् गौतमवचः श्रुत्वा तथास्त्व् इत्य् अब्रवीच् छिवः
अस्याः परतरं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥
75.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing those words of Gautama, Śiva said: ‘So be it!’
There has never been nor will there ever be a tīrtha superior to her.

75.s:
satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ vede ca pariniṣṭhitam
sarveṣāṃ gautamī puṇyā ity uktvāntaradhīyata //
75.d:
सत्यं सत्यं पुनः सत्यं वेदे च परिनिष्ठितम्
सर्वेषां गौतमी पुण्या इत्य् उक्त्वान्तरधीयत ॥
75.m:
It is true, true, and true again, firmly established in the Veda:
the Gautamī is holy to all! Having said this, he vanished.

75.s:
tato gate bhagavati lokapūjite
tadājñayā pūrṇabalaḥ sa gautamaḥ
jaṭāṃ samādāya saridvarāṃ tāṃ
surair vṛto brahmagiriṃ viveśa
75.d:
ततो गते भगवति लोकपूजिते
तदाज्ञया पूर्णबलः स गौतमः
जटां समादाय सरिद्वरां तां
सुरैर् वृतो ब्रह्मगिरिं विवेश
75.m:
Then, when the Lord worshiped by the worlds had departed,
Gautama, filled with strength by his command,
took the matted hair [containing] that best of rivers,
and, surrounded by the gods, entered the mountain of Brahmā.

75.s:
tatas tu gautame prāpte jaṭām ādāya nārada
puṣpavṛṣṭir abhūt tatra samājagmuḥ sureśvarāḥ //
75.d:
ततस् तु गौतमे प्राप्ते जटाम् आदाय नारद
पुष्पवृष्टिर् अभूत् तत्र समाजग्मुः सुरेश्वराः ॥
75.m:
Then, when Gautama arrived holding the matted lock, O Nārada,
a rain of flowers fell there, and the chiefs of the gods gathered.

75.s:
ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyās tathā
jayaśabdena taṃ vipraṃ pūjayanto mudānvitāḥ //
75.d:
ऋषयश् च महाभागा ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियास् तथा
जयशब्देन तं विप्रं पूजयन्तो मुदान्विताः ॥
75.m:
And the eminent sages, the brāhmaṇas and the kṣatriyas,
rejoicing, honored that twice-born with cries of ‘Victory!’

76.s:
nārada uvāca
maheśvarajaṭājuṭād gaṅgām ādāya gautamaḥ
āgatya brahmaṇaḥ puṇye tataḥ kim akarod girau //
76.d:
नारद उवाच
महेश्वरजटाजुटाद् गङ्गाम् आदाय गौतमः
आगत्य ब्रह्मणः पुण्ये ततः किम् अकरोद् गिरौ ॥
76.m:
Nārada said:
Taking the Gaṅgā from the mass of matted hair of the Great Lord
and arriving at the sacred mountain of Brahmā, what did Gautama do then?

76.s:
brahmovāca
ādāya gautamo gaṅgāṃ śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ
pūjito devagandharvais tathā girinivāsibhiḥ //
76.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आदाय गौतमो गङ्गां शुचिः प्रयतमानसः
पूजितो देवगन्धर्वैस् तथा गिरिनिवासिभिः ॥
76.m: Brahmā said: / Having obtained the Gaṅgā, Gautama, pure and restrained in mind, / worshipped by the gods and gandharvas as well as the dwellers of the mountain,

76.s:
girer mūrdhni jaṭāṃ sthāpya smaran devaṃ trilocanam
uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā gaṅgāṃ sa dvijasattamaḥ //
76.d:
गिरेर् मूर्ध्नि जटां स्थाप्य स्मरन् देवं त्रिलोचनम्
उवाच प्राञ्जलिर् भूत्वा गङ्गां स द्विजसत्तमः ॥
76.m: placed the matted lock on the crest of the mountain, and remembering the three-eyed god, / that best of the twice-born, with joined palms, spoke to the Gaṅgā:

76.s:
gautama uvāca
trilocanajaṭodbhūte sarvakāmapradāyini
kṣamasva mātaḥ śāntāsi sukhaṃ yāhi hitaṃ kuru //
76.d:
गौतम उवाच
त्रिलोचनजटोद्भूते सर्वकामप्रदायिनि
क्षमस्व मातः शान्तासि सुखं याहि हितं कुरु ॥
76.m: Gautama said: / "O you who arose from the matted locks of the three-eyed one, granter of all desires, / forgive [me], O mother! You are tranquil; go happily and do good!"

76.s:
brahmovāca
evam uktā gautamena gaṅgā provāca gautamam
divyarūpadharā devī divyasraganulepanā //
76.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्ता गौतमेन गङ्गा प्रोवाच गौतमम्
दिव्यरूपधरा देवी दिव्यस्रगनुलेपना ॥
76.m: Brahmā said: / Addressed thus by Gautama, the goddess Gaṅgā, / bearing a divine form and adorned with divine garlands and ointments, spoke to Gautama:

76.s:
gaṅgovāca
gaccheyaṃ devasadanam athavāpi kamaṇḍalum
rasātalaṃ vā gaccheyaṃ jātas tvaṃ satyavāg asi //
76.d:
गङ्गोवाच
गच्छेयं देवसदनम् अथवापि कमण्डलुम्
रसातलं वा गच्छेयं जातस् त्वं सत्यवाग् असि ॥
76.m: Gaṅgā said: / I may go to the dwelling of the gods, or to the water-pot, / or I may go to the netherworld; you were born truthful in speech.

76.s:
gautama uvāca
trayāṇām upakārārthaṃ lokānāṃ yācitā mayā
śaṃbhunā ca tathā dattā devi tan nānyathā bhavet //
76.d:
गौतम उवाच
त्रयाणाम् उपकारार्थं लोकानां याचिता मया
शंभुना च तथा दत्ता देवि तन् नान्यथा भवेत् ॥
76.m: Gautama said: / You were begged for by me for the benefit of the three worlds, / and given accordingly by Śaṃbhu; O goddess, that cannot be otherwise.

76.s:
brahmovāca
tad gautamavacaḥ śrutvā gaṅgā mene dvijeritam
tredhātmānaṃ vibhajyātha svargamartyarasātale //
76.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् गौतमवचः श्रुत्वा गङ्गा मेने द्विजेरितम्
त्रेधात्मानं विभज्याथ स्वर्गमर्त्यरसातले ॥
76.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing those words of Gautama, Gaṅgā accepted what was spoken by the twice-born. / Then, dividing herself threefold into heaven, earth, and the netherworld,

76.s:
svarge caturdhā vyagamat saptadhā martyamaṇḍale
rasātale caturdhaiva saivaṃ pañcadaśākṛtiḥ //
76.d:
स्वर्गे चतुर्धा व्यगमत् सप्तधा मर्त्यमण्डले
रसातले चतुर्धैव सैवं पञ्चदशाकृतिः ॥
76.m: she went fourfold in heaven, sevenfold on the mortal realm, / and fourfold in the netherworld; thus she has fifteen forms.

76.s:
sarvatra sarvabhūtaiva sarvapāpavināśinī
sarvakāmapradā nityaṃ saiva vede pragīyate //
76.d:
सर्वत्र सर्वभूतैव सर्वपापविनाशिनी
सर्वकामप्रदा नित्यं सैव वेदे प्रगीयते ॥
76.m: Present everywhere as all beings, destroying all sins, / always granting all desires, she alone is celebrated in the Veda.

76.s:
martyā martyagatām eva paśyanti na talaṃ gatām
naiva svargagatāṃ martyāḥ paśyanty ajñānabuddhayaḥ //
76.d:
मर्त्या मर्त्यगताम् एव पश्यन्ति न तलं गताम्
नैव स्वर्गगतां मर्त्याः पश्यन्त्य् अज्ञानबुद्धयः ॥
76.m: Mortals see only the one who has gone to the mortal realm, not the one gone to the nether regions; / nor do mortals, their intellects clouded by ignorance, see the one who has gone to heaven.

76.s:
yāvat sāgaragā devī tāvad devamayī smṛtā
utsṛṣṭā gautamenaiva prāyāt pūrvārṇavaṃ prati //
76.d:
यावत् सागरगा देवी तावद् देवमयी स्मृता
उत्सृष्टा गौतमेनैव प्रायात् पूर्वार्णवं प्रति ॥
76.m: As far as the goddess goes to the ocean, so far is she remembered as composed of the gods. / Released by Gautama, she flowed toward the eastern ocean.

76.s:
tato devarṣibhir juṣṭāṃ mātaraṃ jagataḥ śubhām
gautamo muniśārdūlaḥ pradakṣiṇam athākarot //
76.d:
ततो देवर्षिभिर् जुष्टां मातरं जगतः शुभाम्
गौतमो मुनिशार्दूलः प्रदक्षिणम् अथाकरोत् ॥
76.m: Then Gautama, the tiger among sages, circumambulated / the auspicious mother of the world, frequented by divine sages.

76.s:
trilocanaṃ sureśānaṃ prathamaṃ pūjya gautamaḥ
ubhayos tīrayoḥ snānaṃ karomīti dadhe matim //
76.d:
त्रिलोचनं सुरेशानं प्रथमं पूज्य गौतमः
उभयोस् तीरयोः स्नानं करोमीति दधे मतिम् ॥
76.m: Having first worshipped the three-eyed Lord of the gods, Gautama / resolved: 'I shall bathe on both banks.'

76.s:
smṛtamātras tadā tatrāvirāsīt karuṇārṇavaḥ
tatra snānaṃ kathaṃ sidhyed ity evaṃ śarvam abravīt //
76.d:
स्मृतमात्रस् तदा तत्राविरासीत् करुणार्णवः
तत्र स्नानं कथं सिध्येद् इत्य् एवं शर्वम् अब्रवीत् ॥
76.m: The ocean of compassion appeared there the moment he was remembered. / Gautama spoke thus to Śarva, [asking] how bathing there might be accomplished,

76.s: kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā bhaktinamras trilocanam //
76.d: कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा भक्तिनम्रस् त्रिलोचनम् ॥
76.m: folding his hands in reverence, bowed down in devotion before the Three-eyed Lord.

76.s:
gautama uvāca
devadeva maheśāna tīrthasnānavidhiṃ mama
brūhi samyaṅ maheśāna lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
76.d:
गौतम उवाच
देवदेव महेशान तीर्थस्नानविधिं मम
ब्रूहि सम्यङ् महेशान लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
76.m: Gautama said: / O God of gods, Great Lord, tell me properly / the procedure for bathing in the sacred ford, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.

76.s:
śiva uvāca
maharṣe śṛṇu sarvaṃ ca vidhiṃ godāvarībhavam
pūrvaṃ nāndīmukhaṃ kṛtvā dehaśuddhiṃ vidhāya ca //
76.d:
शिव उवाच
महर्षे शृणु सर्वं च विधिं गोदावरीभवम्
पूर्वं नान्दीमुखं कृत्वा देहशुद्धिं विधाय च ॥
76.m: Śiva said: / O great sage, listen to the entire rite connected with the Godāvarī: / having first performed the rite for the ancestors and the purification of the body,

76.s:
brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā ca teṣām ājñāṃ pragṛhya ca
brahmacaryeṇa gacchanti patitālāpavarjitāḥ //
76.d:
ब्राह्मणान् भोजयित्वा च तेषाम् आज्ञां प्रगृह्य च
ब्रह्मचर्येण गच्छन्ति पतितालापवर्जिताः ॥
76.m: and having fed the brāhmaṇas and received their permission, / they proceed in celibacy, avoiding conversation with the fallen.

76.s:
yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaś caiva susaṃyatam
vidyā tapaś ca kīrtiś ca sa tīrthaphalam aśnute //
76.d:
यस्य हस्तौ च पादौ च मनश् चैव सुसंयतम्
विद्या तपश् च कीर्तिश् च स तीर्थफलम् अश्नुते ॥
76.m: He whose hands, feet, and mind are well restrained, / who has learning, asceticism, and good repute, enjoys the fruit of the sacred ford.

76.s:
bhāvaduṣṭiṃ parityajya svadharmapariniṣṭhitaḥ
śrāntasaṃvāhanaṃ kurvan dadyād annaṃ yathocitam //
76.d:
भावदुष्टिं परित्यज्य स्वधर्मपरिनिष्ठितः
श्रान्तसंवाहनं कुर्वन् दद्याद् अन्नं यथोचितम् ॥
76.m: Casting aside malice of heart, firmly established in his own dharma, / massaging the weary, he should give food as appropriate.

76.s:
akiṃcanebhyaḥ sādhubhyo dadyād vastrāṇi kambalān
śṛṇvan harikathāṃ divyāṃ tathā gaṅgāsamudbhavām
anena vidhinā gacchan samyak tīrthaphalaṃ labhet //
76.d:
अकिंचनेभ्यः साधुभ्यो दद्याद् वस्त्राणि कम्बलान्
शृण्वन् हरिकथां दिव्यां तथा गङ्गासमुद्भवाम्
अनेन विधिना गच्छन् सम्यक् तीर्थफलं लभेत् ॥
76.m: He should give garments and blankets to the destitute and the virtuous, / listening to the divine stories of Hari and the origin of the Gaṅgā; / going by this rule, he obtains the full fruit of the sacred ford.

77.s:
brahmovāca
tryambakaś ca iti prāha gautamaṃ munibhir vṛtam //
77.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
त्र्यम्बकश् च इति प्राह गौतमं मुनिभिर् वृतम् ॥
77.m: Brahmā said: / Tryambaka said this to Gautama, who was surrounded by sages:

77.s:
śiva uvāca
dvihastamātre tīrthāni saṃbhaviṣyanti gautama
sarvatrāhaṃ saṃnihitaḥ sarvakāmapradas tathā //
77.d:
शिव उवाच
द्विहस्तमात्रे तीर्थानि संभविष्यन्ति गौतम
सर्वत्राहं संनिहितः सर्वकामप्रदस् तथा ॥
77.m: Śiva said: / Every two cubits there will be sacred fords, O Gautama; / I am present everywhere, and likewise the granter of all desires.

77.s:
brahmovāca
gaṅgādvāre prayāge ca tathā sāgarasaṃgame
eteṣu puṇyadā puṃsāṃ muktidā sā bhagīrathī //
77.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गङ्गाद्वारे प्रयागे च तथा सागरसंगमे
एतेषु पुण्यदा पुंसां मुक्तिदा सा भगीरथी ॥
77.m: Brahmā said: / At Gaṅgādvāra, at Prayāga, and at the confluence with the ocean— / at these [places] that Bhāgīrathī grants merit and liberation to men.

77.s:
narmadā tu saricchreṣṭhā parvate 'marakaṇṭake
yamunā saṃgatā tatra prabhāse tu sarasvatī //
77.d:
नर्मदा तु सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा पर्वते ऽमरकण्टके
यमुना संगता तत्र प्रभासे तु सरस्वती ॥
77.m: The Narmadā, best of rivers, on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka; / the Yamunā where it conjoins [with the Gaṅgā]; and the Sarasvatī at Prabhāsa;

77.s:
kṛṣṇā bhīmarathī caiva tuṅgabhadrā tu nārada
tisṛṇāṃ saṃgamo yatra tat tīrthaṃ muktidaṃ nṛṇām //
77.d:
कृष्णा भीमरथी चैव तुङ्गभद्रा तु नारद
तिसृणां संगमो यत्र तत् तीर्थं मुक्तिदं नृणाम् ॥
77.m: and the Kṛṣṇā, the Bhīmarathī, and the Tuṅgabhadrā, O Nārada: / where the confluence of these three is, that sacred ford grants liberation to men.

77.s:
payouṣṇī saṃgatā yatra tatratyā tac ca muktidam
iyaṃ tu gautamī vatsa yatra kvāpi mamājñayā //
77.d:
पयोउष्णी संगता यत्र तत्रत्या तच् च मुक्तिदम्
इयं तु गौतमी वत्स यत्र क्वापि ममाज्ञया ॥
77.m: Where the Payoṣṇī has joined, that place too grants liberation. / But this Gautamī, my child, anywhere at all by my command,

77.s:
sarveṣāṃ sarvadā nṝṇāṃ snānān muktiṃ pradāsyati
kiṃcitkāle puṇyatamaṃ kiṃcittīrthaṃ surāgame //
77.d:
सर्वेषां सर्वदा नॄणां स्नानान् मुक्तिं प्रदास्यति
किंचित्काले पुण्यतमं किंचित्तीर्थं सुरागमे ॥
77.m: will grant liberation to all men at all times through bathing. / At certain times a certain sacred ford is most meritorious, according to the scriptures;

77.s:
sarveṣāṃ sarvadā tīrthaṃ gautamī nātra saṃśayaḥ
tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdhakoṭī ca yojanānāṃ śatadvaye //
77.d:
सर्वेषां सर्वदा तीर्थं गौतमी नात्र संशयः
तिस्रः कोट्यो ऽर्धकोटी च योजनानां शतद्वये ॥
77.m: the Gautamī is a sacred ford for all people at all times; there is no doubt of this. / In two hundred yojanas, O tiger among sages, O Gautama,

77.s:
tīrthāni muniśārdūla saṃbhaviṣyanti gautama
iyaṃ māheśvarī gaṅgā gautamī vaiṣṇavīti ca //
77.d:
तीर्थानि मुनिशार्दूल संभविष्यन्ति गौतम
इयं माहेश्वरी गङ्गा गौतमी वैष्णवीति च ॥
77.m: there will be thirty-five million sacred fords. / This is the Māheśvarī Gaṅgā, the Gautamī, the Vaiṣṇavī,

77.s:
brāhmī godāvarī nandā sunandā kāmadāyinī
brahmatejaḥsamānītā sarvapāpapraṇāśanī //
77.d:
ब्राह्मी गोदावरी नन्दा सुनन्दा कामदायिनी
ब्रह्मतेजःसमानीता सर्वपापप्रणाशनी ॥
77.m: the Brāhmī, the Godāvarī, the Nandā, the Sunandā, the giver of desires, / brought by brahmanical splendor, destroying all sins.

77.s:
smaraṇād eva pāpaughahantrī mama sadā priyā
pañcānām api bhūtānām āpaḥ śreṣṭhatvam āgatāḥ //
77.d:
स्मरणाद् एव पापौघहन्त्री मम सदा प्रिया
पञ्चानाम् अपि भूतानाम् आपः श्रेष्ठत्वम् आगताः ॥
77.m: Destroying heaps of sin merely by remembrance, she is ever dear to me. / Even among the five elements, the waters have attained preeminence;

77.s:
tatrāpi tīrthabhūtās tu tasmād āpaḥ parāḥ smṛtāḥ
tāsāṃ bhāgīrathī śreṣṭhā tābhyo 'pi gautamī tathā //
77.d:
तत्रापि तीर्थभूतास् तु तस्माद् आपः पराः स्मृताः
तासां भागीरथी श्रेष्ठा ताभ्यो ऽपि गौतमी तथा ॥
77.m: even among them, those that are sacred fords are remembered as supreme. / Among them, the Bhāgīrathī is best, and even compared to those, the Gautamī is such;

77.s:
ānītā sajaṭā gaṅgā asyā nānyac chubhāvaham
svarge bhuvi tale vāpi tīrthaṃ sarvārthadaṃ mune //
77.d:
आनीता सजटा गङ्गा अस्या नान्यच् छुभावहम्
स्वर्गे भुवि तले वापि तीर्थं सर्वार्थदं मुने ॥
77.m: the Gaṅgā was brought along with [my] matted locks; there is nothing else as auspicious as her, / a sacred ford granting all ends in heaven, on earth, or in the netherworld, O sage.

77.s:
brahmovāca
ity etat kathitaṃ putra gautamāya mahātmane
sākṣād dhareṇa tuṣṭena mayā tava niveditam //
77.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् एतत् कथितं पुत्र गौतमाय महात्मने
साक्षाद् धरेण तुष्टेन मया तव निवेदितम् ॥
77.m: Brahmā said: / Thus this was told to the great-souled Gautama / by Hara himself who was pleased; and by me it has been related to you.

77.s:
evaṃ sā gautamī gaṅgā sarvebhyo 'py adhikā matā
tatsvarūpaṃ ca kathitaṃ kuto 'nyā śravaṇaspṛhā //
77.d:
एवं सा गौतमी गङ्गा सर्वेभ्यो ऽप्य् अधिका मता
तत्स्वरूपं च कथितं कुतो ऽन्या श्रवणस्पृहा ॥
77.m: Thus that Gautamī Gaṅgā is considered superior to all; / and her true nature has been told. What other desire to hear could there be?

78.s:
nārada uvāca
dvividhā saiva gaditā ekāpi surasattama
eko bhedas tu kathito brāhmaṇenāhṛto yataḥ //
78.d:
नारद उवाच
द्विविधा सैव गदिता एकापि सुरसत्तम
एको भेदस् तु कथितो ब्राह्मणेनाहृतो यतः ॥
78.m: Nārada said: / She has been described as twofold, though she is one, O best of gods; / one division has been told, since it was brought down by the brāhmaṇa.

78.s:
kṣatriyeṇāparo 'py aṃśo jaṭāsv eva vyavasthitaḥ
bhavasya devadevasya āhṛtas tad vadasva me //
78.d:
क्षत्रियेणापरो ऽप्य् अंशो जटास्व् एव व्यवस्थितः
भवस्य देवदेवस्य आहृतस् तद् वदस्व मे ॥
78.m: Tell me how the other portion, resting in the matted locks / of Bhava, the God of gods, was brought down by the kṣatriya.

78.s:
brahmovāca
vaivasvatānvaye jāta ikṣvākukulasaṃbhavaḥ
purā vai sagaro nāma rājāsīd atidhārmikaḥ //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वैवस्वतान्वये जात इक्ष्वाकुकुलसंभवः
पुरा वै सगरो नाम राजासीद् अतिधार्मिकः ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Formerly there was a king named Sagara, born in the lineage of Vivasvat / and originating from the race of Ikṣvāku, who was exceedingly righteous,

78.s:
yajvā dānaparo nityaṃ dharmācāravicāravān
tasya bhāryādvayaṃ cāsīt patibhaktiparāyaṇam //
78.d:
यज्वा दानपरो नित्यं धर्माचारविचारवान्
तस्य भार्याद्वयं चासीत् पतिभक्तिपरायणम् ॥
78.m: a performer of sacrifices, constantly devoted to charity, endowed with judgment in lawful conduct. / He had two wives, who were devoted in service to their husband.

78.s:
tasya vai saṃtatir nābhūd iti cintāparo 'bhavat
vasiṣṭhaṃ gṛham āhūya saṃpūjya vidhivat tataḥ //
78.d:
तस्य वै संततिर् नाभूद् इति चिन्तापरो ऽभवत्
वसिष्ठं गृहम् आहूय संपूज्य विधिवत् ततः ॥
78.m: He had no offspring, and so he became filled with anxiety. / Having invited Vasiṣṭha to his house and worshipped him according to rule,

78.s:
uvāca vacanaṃ rājā saṃtateḥ kāraṇaṃ prati
iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dhyātvā rājānam abravīt //
78.d:
उवाच वचनं राजा संततेः कारणं प्रति
इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ध्यात्वा राजानम् अब्रवीत् ॥
78.m: the king then spoke words concerning the cause of offspring. / Hearing his words and contemplating, he spoke to the king:

78.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
sapatnīkaḥ sadā rājann ṛṣipūjāparo bhava //
78.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
सपत्नीकः सदा राजन्न् ऋषिपूजापरो भव ॥
78.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Together with your wives, O king, be ever devoted to the worship of sages.

78.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā sa munir vipra yathāsthānaṃ jagāma ha
ekadā tasya rājarṣer gṛham āgāt taponidhiḥ //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा स मुनिर् विप्र यथास्थानं जगाम ह
एकदा तस्य राजर्षेर् गृहम् आगात् तपोनिधिः ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, O twice-born, that sage went to his abode. / Once, a treasury of asceticism came to the royal sage’s house.

78.s:
tasyarṣeḥ pūjanaṃ cakre sa saṃtuṣṭo 'bravīd vacam
varaṃ brūhi mahābhāgety ukte putrān sa cāvṛṇot //
78.d:
तस्यर्षेः पूजनं चक्रे स संतुष्टो ऽब्रवीद् वचम्
वरं ब्रूहि महाभागेत्य् उक्ते पुत्रान् स चावृणोत् ॥
78.m: He worshipped that sage; well-pleased, the sage said: / 'Choose a boon, O fortunate one.' When this was said, he chose sons.

78.s:
sa muniḥ prāha rājānam ekasyāṃ vaṃśadhārakaḥ
putro bhūyāt tathānyasyāṃ ṣaṣṭisāhasrakaṃ sutāḥ //
78.d:
स मुनिः प्राह राजानम् एकस्यां वंशधारकः
पुत्रो भूयात् तथान्यस्यां षष्टिसाहस्रकं सुताः ॥
78.m: That sage said to the king: 'On one wife let there be a son / who sustains the lineage, and on the other sixty thousand sons.'

78.s:
varaṃ dattvā munau yāte putrā jātāḥ sahasraśaḥ
sa yajñān subahūṃś cakre hayamedhān sudakṣiṇān //
78.d:
वरं दत्त्वा मुनौ याते पुत्रा जाताः सहस्रशः
स यज्ञान् सुबहूंश् चक्रे हयमेधान् सुदक्षिणान् ॥
78.m: When the sage had gone after granting the boon, thousands of sons were born. / He performed very many sacrifices, horse sacrifices with generous sacrificial gifts.

78.s:
ekasmin hayamedhe vai dīkṣito vidhivan nṛpaḥ
putrān nyayojayad rājā sasainyān hayarakṣaṇe //
78.d:
एकस्मिन् हयमेधे वै दीक्षितो विधिवन् नृपः
पुत्रान् न्ययोजयद् राजा ससैन्यान् हयरक्षणे ॥
78.m: Consecrated according to rule for one horse sacrifice, / the king appointed his sons, accompanied by the army, to protect the horse.

78.s:
kvacid antaram āsādya hayaṃ jahre śatakratuḥ
mārgamāṇāś ca te putrā naivāpaśyan hayaṃ tadā //
78.d:
क्वचिद् अन्तरम् आसाद्य हयं जह्रे शतक्रतुः
मार्गमाणाश् च ते पुत्रा नैवापश्यन् हयं तदा ॥
78.m: Finding an opening somewhere, the lord of a hundred sacrifices carried off the horse; / and those sons, searching, did not find the horse then.

78.s:
sahasrāṇāṃ tathā ṣaṣṭir nānāyuddhaviśāradāḥ
teṣu paśyatsu rakṣāṃsi putreṣu sagarasya hi //
78.d:
सहस्राणां तथा षष्टिर् नानायुद्धविशारदाः
तेषु पश्यत्सु रक्षांसि पुत्रेषु सगरस्य हि ॥
78.m: The sixty thousand [sons], skilled in various kinds of warfare— / while those sons of Sagara were watching, the demons [stole it].

78.s:
prokṣitaṃ tad dhayaṃ nītvā te rasātalam āgaman
rākṣasān māyayā yuktān naivāpaśyanta sāgarāḥ //
78.d:
प्रोक्षितं तद् धयं नीत्वा ते रसातलम् आगमन्
राक्षसान् मायया युक्तान् नैवापश्यन्त सागराः ॥
78.m: Taking that consecrated horse, they went to the netherworld. / The sons of Sagara did not see the rākṣasas endowed with illusory power.

78.s:
na dṛṣṭvā te hayaṃ putrāḥ sagarasya balīyasaḥ
itaś cetaś carantas te naivāpaśyan hayaṃ tadā //
78.d:
न दृष्ट्वा ते हयं पुत्राः सगरस्य बलीयसः
इतश् चेतश् चरन्तस् ते नैवापश्यन् हयं तदा ॥
78.m: Not seeing the horse, the mighty sons of Sagara / wandered here and there, but did not see the horse then.

78.s:
devalokaṃ tadā jagmuḥ parvatāṃś ca sarāṃsi ca
vanāni ca vicinvanto naivāpaśyan hayaṃ tadā //
78.d:
देवलोकं तदा जग्मुः पर्वतांश् च सरांसि च
वनानि च विचिन्वन्तो नैवापश्यन् हयं तदा ॥
78.m: Then they went to the world of the gods, and searching mountains, lakes, / and forests, they did not see the horse then.

78.s:
kṛtasvastyayano rājā ṛtvigbhiḥ kṛtamaṅgalaḥ
adṛṣṭvā tu paśuṃ ramyaṃ rājā cintām upeyivān //
78.d:
कृतस्वस्त्ययनो राजा ऋत्विग्भिः कृतमङ्गलः
अदृष्ट्वा तु पशुं रम्यं राजा चिन्ताम् उपेयिवान् ॥
78.m: The king, for whom rites for welfare and auspicious blessings had been performed by the sacrificial priests, / fell into anxiety upon not seeing the lovely victim.

78.s:
aṭantaḥ sāgarāḥ sarve devalokam upāgaman
hayaṃ tam anucinvantas tatrāpi na hayo 'bhavat //
78.d:
अटन्तः सागराः सर्वे देवलोकम् उपागमन्
हयं तम् अनुचिन्वन्तस् तत्रापि न हयो ऽभवत् ॥
78.m: All the sons of Sagara, roaming about, reached the world of the gods, / searching for that horse; but the horse was not there either.

78.s:
tato mahīṃ samājagmuḥ parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca
tatrāpi ca hayaṃ naiva dṛṣṭavanto nṛpātmajāḥ //
78.d:
ततो महीं समाजग्मुः पर्वतांश् च वनानि च
तत्रापि च हयं नैव दृष्टवन्तो नृपात्मजाः ॥
78.m: Then they came to the earth, to the mountains and forests; / there too the king's sons did not see the horse at all.

78.s:
etasminn antare tatra daivī vāg abhavat tadā
rasātale hayo baddha āste nānyatra sāgarāḥ //
78.d:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र दैवी वाग् अभवत् तदा
रसातले हयो बद्ध आस्ते नान्यत्र सागराः ॥
78.m: In the meantime, a divine voice arose there: / “The horse is bound in the netherworld, O sons of Sagara, nowhere else!”

78.s:
iti śrutvā tato vākyaṃ gantukāmā rasātalam
akhanan pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ paritaḥ sāgarās tataḥ //
78.d:
इति श्रुत्वा ततो वाक्यं गन्तुकामा रसातलम्
अखनन् पृथिवीं सर्वां परितः सागरास् ततः ॥
78.m: Hearing that speech, desirous of going to the netherworld, / the sons of Sagara then dug up the entire earth on all sides.

78.s:
te kṣudhārtā mṛdaṃ śuṣkāṃ bhakṣayantas tv aharniśam
nyakhanaṃś cāpi jagmuś ca satvarās te rasātalam //
78.d:
ते क्षुधार्ता मृदं शुष्कां भक्षयन्तस् त्व् अहर्निशम्
न्यखनंश् चापि जग्मुश् च सत्वरास् ते रसातलम् ॥
78.m: Afflicted by hunger, eating dry earth day and night, / they dug deep and swiftly went down to the netherworld.

78.s:
tān āgatān bhūpasutān sāgarān balinaḥ kṛtīn
śrutvā rakṣāṃsi saṃtrastā vyagaman kapilāntikam //
78.d:
तान् आगतान् भूपसुतान् सागरान् बलिनः कृतीन्
श्रुत्वा रक्षांसि संत्रस्ता व्यगमन् कपिलान्तिकम् ॥
78.m: Hearing that the king's sons had arrived—the sons of Sagara, strong and capable— / the rākṣasas were terrified and went near Kapila.

78.s:
kapilo 'pi mahāprājñas tatra śete rasātale
purā ca sādhitaṃ tena devānāṃ kāryam uttamam //
78.d:
कपिलो ऽपि महाप्राज्ञस् तत्र शेते रसातले
पुरा च साधितं तेन देवानां कार्यम् उत्तमम् ॥
78.m: Kapila too, the very wise, was sleeping there in the netherworld. / Long ago, an excellent task for the gods had been accomplished by him.

78.s:
vinidreṇa tataḥ śrāntaḥ siddhe kārye surān prati
abravīt kapilaḥ śrīmān nidrāsthānaṃ prayacchatha //
78.d:
विनिद्रेण ततः श्रान्तः सिद्धे कार्ये सुरान् प्रति
अब्रवीत् कपिलः श्रीमान् निद्रास्थानं प्रयच्छथ ॥
78.m: Weary then from sleeplessness, when the task was accomplished, / the glorious Kapila spoke to the gods: “Grant me a place to sleep.

78.s:
rasātalaṃ dadus tasmai punar āha surān muniḥ
yo mām utthāpayen mando bhasmī bhūyāc ca satvaram //
78.d:
रसातलं ददुस् तस्मै पुनर् आह सुरान् मुनिः
यो माम् उत्थापयेन् मन्दो भस्मी भूयाच् च सत्वरम् ॥
78.m: They gave him the netherworld. Again the sage said to the gods: / “Whoever foolishly wakes me up shall quickly be reduced to ashes.

78.s:
tataḥ śaye talagato no cen na svapna eva hi
tathety uktaḥ suragaṇais tatra śete rasātale //
78.d:
ततः शये तलगतो नो चेन् न स्वप्न एव हि
तथेत्य् उक्तः सुरगणैस् तत्र शेते रसातले ॥
78.m: Then I shall sleep, gone to the bottom; otherwise there is no sleep at all.” / Told “So be it” by the hosts of gods, he was sleeping there in the netherworld.

78.s:
tasya prabhāvaṃ te jñātvā rākṣasā māyayā yutāḥ
sāgarāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vadhopāyaṃ pracakrire //
78.d:
तस्य प्रभावं ते ज्ञात्वा राक्षसा मायया युताः
सागराणां च सर्वेषां वधोपायं प्रचक्रिरे ॥
78.m: Knowing his power, the rākṣasas endowed with illusory power / devised a means for the destruction of all the sons of Sagara.

78.s:
vinā yuddhena te bhītā rākṣasāḥ satvarās tadā
āgatya yatra sa muniḥ kapilaḥ kopano mahān //
78.d:
विना युद्धेन ते भीता राक्षसाः सत्वरास् तदा
आगत्य यत्र स मुनिः कपिलः कोपनो महान् ॥
78.m: Afraid without a battle, those rākṣasas then quickly / arrived where that sage Kapila, prone to great anger, was.

78.s:
śirodeśe hayaṃ te vai baddhvātha tvarayānvitāḥ
dūre sthitvā mauninaś ca prekṣantaḥ kiṃ bhaved iti //
78.d:
शिरोदेशे हयं ते वै बद्ध्वाथ त्वरयान्विताः
दूरे स्थित्वा मौनिनश् च प्रेक्षन्तः किं भवेद् इति ॥
78.m: Indeed, having swiftly bound the horse near his head, / they stood silently at a distance, watching what would happen.

78.s:
tatas tu sāgarāḥ sarve nirviśanto rasātalam
dadṛśus te hayaṃ baddhaṃ śayānaṃ puruṣaṃ tathā //
78.d:
ततस् तु सागराः सर्वे निर्विशन्तो रसातलम्
ददृशुस् ते हयं बद्धं शयानं पुरुषं तथा ॥
78.m: Then all the sons of Sagara, entering the netherworld, / saw the bound horse and also the sleeping man.

78.s:
taṃ menire ca hartāraṃ kratuhantāram eva ca
enaṃ hatvā mahāpāpaṃ nayāmo 'śvaṃ nṛpāntikam //
78.d:
तं मेनिरे च हर्तारं क्रतुहन्तारम् एव च
एनं हत्वा महापापं नयामो ऽश्वं नृपान्तिकम् ॥
78.m: And they considered him the thief and the destroyer of the sacrifice: / “Having slain this great sinner, let us lead the horse to the king.”

78.s:
kecid ūcuḥ paśuṃ baddhaṃ nayāmo 'nena kiṃ phalam
tadāhur apare śūrā rājānaḥ śāsakā vayam //
78.d:
केचिद् ऊचुः पशुं बद्धं नयामो ऽनेन किं फलम्
तदाहुर् अपरे शूरा राजानः शासका वयम् ॥
78.m: Some said, “Let us take the bound victim; what is the use of him?” / Then other heroes said, “We are kings and rulers!

78.s:
utthāpyainaṃ mahāpāpaṃ hanmaḥ kṣātreṇa varcasā
te taṃ jaghnur muniṃ pādair bruvanto niṣṭhurāṇi ca //
78.d:
उत्थाप्यैनं महापापं हन्मः क्षात्रेण वर्चसा
ते तं जघ्नुर् मुनिं पादैर् ब्रुवन्तो निष्ठुराणि च ॥
78.m: Having awakened this great sinner, let us strike him with kṣatriya might!” / Speaking harsh words, they struck that sage with their feet.

78.s:
tataḥ kopena mahatā kapilo munisattamaḥ
sāgarān īkṣayām āsa tān kopād bhasmasāt karot //
78.d:
ततः कोपेन महता कपिलो मुनिसत्तमः
सागरान् ईक्षयाम् आस तान् कोपाद् भस्मसात् करोत् ॥
78.m: Then, with great anger, Kapila, the best of sages, / looked upon the sons of Sagara and reduced them to ashes out of wrath.

78.s:
jajvalus te tatas tatra sāgarāḥ sarva eva hi
tat tu sarvaṃ na jānāti dīkṣitaḥ sagaro nṛpaḥ //
78.d:
जज्वलुस् ते ततस् तत्र सागराः सर्व एव हि
तत् तु सर्वं न जानाति दीक्षितः सगरो नृपः ॥
78.m: Then all the sons of Sagara burned right there. / But King Sagara, consecrated [for the sacrifice], did not know any of that.

78.s:
nāradaḥ kathayām āsa sagarāya mahātmane
kapilasya tu saṃsthānaṃ hayasyāpi tu saṃsthitim //
78.d:
नारदः कथयाम् आस सगराय महात्मने
कपिलस्य तु संस्थानं हयस्यापि तु संस्थितिम् ॥
78.m: Nārada related to the great-souled Sagara / the abode of Kapila and the location of the horse,

78.s:
rākṣasānāṃ tu vikṛtiṃ sāgarāṇāṃ ca nāśanam
tataś cintāparo rājā kartavyaṃ nāvabudhyata //
78.d:
राक्षसानां तु विकृतिं सागराणां च नाशनम्
ततश् चिन्तापरो राजा कर्तव्यं नावबुध्यत ॥
78.m: as well as the deception of the rākṣasas and the destruction of the sons of Sagara. / Thereupon the king, overcome with grief, did not know what was to be done.

78.s:
aparo 'pi sutaś cāsīd asamañjā iti śrutaḥ
sa tu bālāṃs tathā paurān maurkhyāt kṣipati cāmbhasi //
78.d:
अपरो ऽपि सुतश् चासीद् असमञ्जा इति श्रुतः
स तु बालांस् तथा पौरान् मौर्ख्यात् क्षिपति चाम्भसि ॥
78.m: There was also another son, known as Asamañjas; / he, however, out of foolishness, used to throw children and citizens into the water.

78.s:
sagaro 'py atha vijñaptaḥ pauraiḥ saṃmilitais tadā
durnayaṃ tasya taṃ jñātvā tataḥ kruddho 'bravīn nṛpaḥ //
78.d:
सगरो ऽप्य् अथ विज्ञप्तः पौरैः संमिलितैस् तदा
दुर्नयं तस्य तं ज्ञात्वा ततः क्रुद्धो ऽब्रवीन् नृपः ॥
78.m: Then Sagara was petitioned by the citizens gathered together; / learning of his wicked misconduct, the king angrily said

78.s:
svān amātyāṃs tadā rājā deśatyāgaṃ karotv ayam
asamañjāḥ kṣatradharmatyāgī vai bālaghātakaḥ //
78.d:
स्वान् अमात्यांस् तदा राजा देशत्यागं करोत्व् अयम्
असमञ्जाः क्षत्रधर्मत्यागी वै बालघातकः ॥
78.m: to his ministers then: “Let this one be banished from the country! / Asamañjas has abandoned the kṣatriya duty and is indeed a slayer of children.”

78.s:
sagarasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvāmātyās tvarānvitāḥ
tatyajur nṛpateḥ putram asamañjā gato vanam //
78.d:
सगरस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वामात्यास् त्वरान्विताः
तत्यजुर् नृपतेः पुत्रम् असमञ्जा गतो वनम् ॥
78.m: Hearing that command of Sagara, the ministers quickly / banished the king's son; Asamañjas went to the forest.

78.s:
sāgarā brahmaśāpena naṣṭāḥ sarve rasātale
eko 'pi ca vanaṃ prāpta idānīṃ kā gatir mama //
78.d:
सागरा ब्रह्मशापेन नष्टाः सर्वे रसातले
एको ऽपि च वनं प्राप्त इदानीं का गतिर् मम ॥
78.m: [Sagara thought:] “The sons of Sagara have all perished in the netherworld through a brahman's curse, / and the one [left] has gone to the forest; what now is my refuge?”

78.s:
aṃśumān iti vikhyātaḥ putras tasyāsamañjasaḥ
ānāyya bālakaṃ rājā kāryaṃ tasmai nyavedayat //
78.d:
अंशुमान् इति विख्यातः पुत्रस् तस्यासमञ्जसः
आनाय्य बालकं राजा कार्यं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ॥
78.m: The son of that Asamañjas was renowned as Aṃśumat. / Summoning the boy, the king entrusted the duty to him.

78.s:
kapilaṃ ca samārādhya aṃśumān api bālakaḥ
sagarāya hayaṃ prādāt tataḥ pūrṇo 'bhavat kratuḥ //
78.d:
कपिलं च समाराध्य अंशुमान् अपि बालकः
सगराय हयं प्रादात् ततः पूर्णो ऽभवत् क्रतुः ॥
78.m: And propitiating Kapila, the boy Aṃśumat too / gave the horse to Sagara; then the sacrifice was completed.

78.s:
tasyāpi putras tejasvī dilīpa iti dhārmikaḥ
tasyāpi putro matimān bhagīratha iti śrutaḥ //
78.d:
तस्यापि पुत्रस् तेजस्वी दिलीप इति धार्मिकः
तस्यापि पुत्रो मतिमान् भगीरथ इति श्रुतः ॥
78.m: His son was also radiant and righteous, named Dilīpa; / his son was the wise one known as Bhagīratha.

78.s:
pitāmahānāṃ sarveṣāṃ gatiṃ śrutvā suduḥkhitaḥ
sagaraṃ nṛpaśārdūlaṃ papraccha vinayānvitaḥ //
78.d:
पितामहानां सर्वेषां गतिं श्रुत्वा सुदुःखितः
सगरं नृपशार्दूलं पप्रच्छ विनयान्वितः ॥
78.m: Hearing of the fate of all his grandfathers, extremely distressed, / he asked Sagara, the tiger among kings, with humility:

78.s:
sāgarāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ niṣkṛtis tu kathaṃ bhavet
bhagīrathaṃ nṛpaḥ prāha kapilo vetti putraka //
78.d:
सागराणां तु सर्वेषां निष्कृतिस् तु कथं भवेत्
भगीरथं नृपः प्राह कपिलो वेत्ति पुत्रक ॥
78.m: “How could there be atonement for all the sons of Sagara?” / The king said to Bhagīratha: “Kapila knows, my child.”

78.s:
tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bālaḥ prāyād rasātalam
kapilaṃ ca namaskṛtvā sarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayat //
78.d:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा बालः प्रायाद् रसातलम्
कपिलं च नमस्कृत्वा सर्वं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ॥
78.m: Hearing that word of his, the boy went to the netherworld, / and having bowed to Kapila, he related everything to him.

78.s:
sa munis tu ciraṃ dhyātvā tapasārādhya śaṃkaram
jaṭājalena svapitṝn āplāvya nṛpasattama //
78.d:
स मुनिस् तु चिरं ध्यात्वा तपसाराध्य शंकरम्
जटाजलेन स्वपितॄन् आप्लाव्य नृपसत्तम ॥
78.m: Meditating for a long time, that sage [said]: “Having propitiated Śaṅkara through austerities, / and bathing your ancestors with the water from his matted hair, O best of kings,

78.s:
tataḥ kṛtārtho bhavitā tvaṃ ca te pitaras tathā
tathā karomīti muniṃ praṇamya punar abravīt //
78.d:
ततः कृतार्थो भविता त्वं च ते पितरस् तथा
तथा करोमीति मुनिं प्रणम्य पुनर् अब्रवीत् ॥
78.m: then you will have achieved your goal, and so will your fathers.” / Saying “I will do so,” and bowing to the sage, he spoke again:

78.s: kva gacche 'haṃ muniśreṣṭha kartavyaṃ cāpi tad vada //
78.d: क्व गच्छे ऽहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ कर्तव्यं चापि तद् वद ॥
78.m: “Where should I go, O best of sages, and tell me what is to be done.”

78.s:
kapila uvāca
kailāsaṃ taṃ naraśreṣṭha gatvā stuhi maheśvaram
tapaḥ kuru yathāśakti tataś cepsitam āpsyasi //
78.d:
कपिल उवाच
कैलासं तं नरश्रेष्ठ गत्वा स्तुहि महेश्वरम्
तपः कुरु यथाशक्ति ततश् चेप्सितम् आप्स्यसि ॥
78.m: Kapila said: / “Going to Mount Kailāsa, O best of men, praise Maheśvara; / perform austerities according to your power, and then you will attain your desire.”

78.s:
brahmovāca
tac chrutvā sa muner vākyaṃ muniṃ natvā tv agān nagam
kailāsaṃ sa śucir bhūtvā bālo bālakriyānvitaḥ
tapase niścayaṃ kṛtvā uvāca sa bhagīrathaḥ //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तच् छ्रुत्वा स मुनेर् वाक्यं मुनिं नत्वा त्व् अगान् नगम्
कैलासं स शुचिर् भूत्वा बालो बालक्रियान्वितः
तपसे निश्चयं कृत्वा उवाच स भगीरथः ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that word of the sage and bowing to the sage, he went to the mountain / Kailāsa; having become pure, the boy, although behaving as a child, / resolved upon austerities, and that Bhagīratha spoke:

78.s:
bhagīratha uvāca
bālo 'haṃ bālabuddhiś ca bālacandradhara prabho
nāhaṃ kimapi jānāmi tataḥ prīto bhava prabho //
78.d:
भगीरथ उवाच
बालो ऽहं बालबुद्धिश् च बालचन्द्रधर प्रभो
नाहं किमपि जानामि ततः प्रीतो भव प्रभो ॥
78.m: Bhagīratha said: / “I am a child, with the intellect of a child, O Lord who bears the crescent moon! / I do not know anything; therefore, be pleased, O Lord!

78.s:
vāgbhir manobhiḥ kṛtibhiḥ kadācin
mamopakurvanti hite ratā ye
tebhyo hitārthaṃ tv iha cāmareśa
somaṃ namasyāmi surādipūjyam
78.d:
वाग्भिर् मनोभिः कृतिभिः कदाचिन्
ममोपकुर्वन्ति हिते रता ये
तेभ्यो हितार्थं त्व् इह चामरेश
सोमं नमस्यामि सुरादिपूज्यम्
78.m: Those who, intent on my welfare, ever assist me / through words, minds, and deeds— / for their welfare in this world, O Lord of immortals, / I bow to Soma, who is worshipped by the gods and others.

78.s:
utpādito yair abhivardhitaś ca
samānagotraś ca samānadharmā
teṣām abhīṣṭāni śivaḥ karotu
bālendumauliṃ praṇato 'smi nityam
78.d:
उत्पादितो यैर् अभिवर्धितश् च
समानगोत्रश् च समानधर्मा
तेषाम् अभीष्टानि शिवः करोतु
बालेन्दुमौलिं प्रणतो ऽस्मि नित्यम्
78.m: May Śiva grant the desires of those by whom I was begotten / and raised, belonging to the same lineage and the same dharma! / I ever bow to the one who has the young crescent moon upon his crest.”

78.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ tu bruvatas tasya purastād abhavac chivaḥ
vareṇa cchandayāno vai bhagīratham uvāca ha //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं तु ब्रुवतस् तस्य पुरस्ताद् अभवच् छिवः
वरेण च्छन्दयानो वै भगीरथम् उवाच ह ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / While he was speaking thus, Śiva appeared before him, / and tempting Bhagīratha with a boon, he spoke:

78.s:
śiva uvāca
yan na sādhyaṃ suragaṇair deyaṃ tat te mayā dhruvam
vadasva nirbhayo bhūtvā bhagīratha mahāmate //
78.d:
शिव उवाच
यन् न साध्यं सुरगणैर् देयं तत् ते मया ध्रुवम्
वदस्व निर्भयो भूत्वा भगीरथ महामते ॥
78.m: Śiva said: / “What cannot be accomplished by the host of gods shall surely be granted to you by me; / speak without fear, O highly intelligent Bhagīratha!”

78.s:
brahmovāca
bhagīrathaḥ praṇamyeśaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ provāca śaṃkaram //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भगीरथः प्रणम्येशं हृष्टः प्रोवाच शंकरम् ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Bowing to the Lord, delighted, Bhagīratha addressed Śaṅkara:

78.s:
bhagīratha uvāca
jaṭāsthitāṃ pitṝṇāṃ me pāvanāya saridvarām
tām eva dehi deveśa sarvam āptaṃ tato bhavet //
78.d:
भगीरथ उवाच
जटास्थितां पितॄणां मे पावनाय सरिद्वराम्
ताम् एव देहि देवेश सर्वम् आप्तं ततो भवेत् ॥
78.m: Bhagīratha said: / "Give me that very best of rivers resting in your matted hair, O Lord of gods, / for the purification of my ancestors; then everything will have been gained."

78.s:
brahmovāca
maheśo 'pi vihasyātha bhagīratham uvāca ha //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
महेशो ऽपि विहस्याथ भगीरथम् उवाच ह ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Thereupon the Great Lord also smiled and addressed Bhagīratha:

78.s:
śiva uvāca
dattā mayeyaṃ te putra punas tāṃ stuhi suvrata //
78.d:
शिव उवाच
दत्ता मयेयं ते पुत्र पुनस् तां स्तुहि सुव्रत ॥
78.m: Śiva said: / "She is given by me to you, my son; praise her once again, O you of noble vows."

78.s:
brahmovāca
tad devavacanaṃ śrutvā tadarthaṃ tu tapo mahat
stutiṃ cakāra gaṅgāyā bhaktyā prayatamānasaḥ //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् देववचनं श्रुत्वा तदर्थं तु तपो महत्
स्तुतिं चकार गङ्गाया भक्त्या प्रयतमानसः ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing those words of the god, [undertaking] great asceticism for her sake, / he offered praise to the Gaṅgā with devotion, his mind concentrated.

78.s:
tasyā api prasādaṃ ca prāpya bālo 'py abālavat
gaṅgāṃ maheśvarāt prāptām ādāyāgād rasātalam //
78.d:
तस्या अपि प्रसादं च प्राप्य बालो ऽप्य् अबालवत्
गङ्गां महेश्वरात् प्राप्ताम् आदायागाद् रसातलम् ॥
78.m: Having obtained her grace too, though a boy, yet acting like no boy, / he took the Gaṅgā received from the Great Lord and went to Rasātala.

78.s:
nyavedayat sa munaye kapilāya mahātmane
yathoditaprakāreṇa gaṅgāṃ saṃsthāpya yatnataḥ //
78.d:
न्यवेदयत् स मुनये कपिलाय महात्मने
यथोदितप्रकारेण गङ्गां संस्थाप्य यत्नतः ॥
78.m: He announced it to the great-souled sage Kapila, / having painstakingly established the Gaṅgā in the prescribed manner.

78.s: pradakṣiṇam athāvartya kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'bravīt //
78.d: प्रदक्षिणम् अथावर्त्य कृताञ्जलिपुटो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
78.m: Then, having circumambulated [him] clockwise, with folded hands he spoke:

78.s:
bhagīratha uvāca
devi me pitaraḥ śāpāt kapilasya mahāmuneḥ
prāptās te vigatiṃ mātas tasmāt tān pātum arhasi //
78.d:
भगीरथ उवाच
देवि मे पितरः शापात् कपिलस्य महामुनेः
प्राप्तास् ते विगतिं मातस् तस्मात् तान् पातुम् अर्हसि ॥
78.m: Bhagīratha said: / "O goddess, by the curse of the great sage Kapila my ancestors / have met their ruin; therefore, O Mother, you ought to protect them."

78.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā suranadī sarveṣām upakārikā
lokānām upakārārthaṃ pitṝṇāṃ pāvanāya ca //
78.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा सुरनदी सर्वेषाम् उपकारिका
लोकानाम् उपकारार्थं पितॄणां पावनाय च ॥
78.m: Brahmā said: / Saying, "So be it," the river of the gods, benefactress of all, / for the benefit of the worlds and for the purification of the ancestors,

78.s:
agastyapītasyāmbhodheḥ pūraṇāya viśeṣataḥ
smaraṇād eva pāpānāṃ nāśāya suranimnagā //
78.d:
अगस्त्यपीतस्याम्भोधेः पूरणाय विशेषतः
स्मरणाद् एव पापानां नाशाय सुरनिम्नगा ॥
78.m: especially for the refilling of the ocean drunk dry by Agastya, / and for the destruction of sins merely by being remembered, the river of the gods

78.s:
bhagīrathoditaṃ cakre rasātalatale sthitān
bhasmībhūtān nṛpasutān sāgarāṃś ca viśeṣataḥ //
78.d:
भगीरथोदितं चक्रे रसातलतले स्थितान्
भस्मीभूतान् नृपसुतान् सागरांश् च विशेषतः ॥
78.m: did as Bhagīratha had asked. Resting on the floor of Rasātala, / especially for the sons of the king, the sons of Sagara, who had been turned to ash,

78.s:
vinirdagdhān athāplāvya khātapūram athākarot
tato meruṃ samāplāvya sthitāṃ bālo 'bravīn nṛpaḥ //
78.d:
विनिर्दग्धान् अथाप्लाव्य खातपूरम् अथाकरोत्
ततो मेरुं समाप्लाव्य स्थितां बालो ऽब्रवीन् नृपः ॥
78.m: inundating those who were burnt up, she filled up the excavated trench. / Then, inundating Meru, to her as she stood, the boy king spoke:

78.s:
karmabhūmau tvayā bhāvyaṃ tathety āgād dhimālayam
himavatparvatāt puṇyād bhārataṃ varṣam abhyagāt //
78.d:
कर्मभूमौ त्वया भाव्यं तथेत्य् आगाद् धिमालयम्
हिमवत्पर्वतात् पुण्याद् भारतं वर्षम् अभ्यगात् ॥
78.m: "You must abide in the land of works." Saying, "So be it," she went to the Himālaya. / From the holy Himavat mountain she came to Bhārata-varṣa.

78.s:
tanmadhyataḥ puṇyanadī prāyāt pūrvārṇavaṃ prati
evam eṣāpi te proktā gaṅgā kṣātrā mahāmune //
78.d:
तन्मध्यतः पुण्यनदी प्रायात् पूर्वार्णवं प्रति
एवम् एषापि ते प्रोक्ता गङ्गा क्षात्रा महामुने ॥
78.m: From its midst the holy river flowed toward the eastern ocean. / Thus this [river] also, the royal Gaṅgā, has been described to you, O great sage.

78.s:
māheśvarī vaiṣṇavī ca saiva brāhmī ca pāvanī
bhāgīrathī devanadī himavacchikharāśrayā //
78.d:
माहेश्वरी वैष्णवी च सैव ब्राह्मी च पावनी
भागीरथी देवनदी हिमवच्छिखराश्रया ॥
78.m: Belonging to Maheśvara, belonging to Viṣṇu, and she herself belonging to Brahmā, the purifier, / the river of the gods, the Bhāgīrathī, resting on the peaks of the Himavat,

78.s:
maheśvarajaṭāvāri evaṃ dvaividhyam āgatam
vindhyasya dakṣiṇe gaṅgā gautamī sā nigadyate
uttare sāpi vindhyasya bhāgīrathy abhidhīyate //
78.d:
महेश्वरजटावारि एवं द्वैविध्यम् आगतम्
विन्ध्यस्य दक्षिणे गङ्गा गौतमी सा निगद्यते
उत्तरे सापि विन्ध्यस्य भागीरथ्य् अभिधीयते ॥
78.m: the water from the Great Lord's matted hair, has thus attained a twofold nature: / south of the Vindhya, that Gaṅgā is called the Gautamī; / north of the Vindhya, she is termed the Bhāgīrathī.

79.s:
nārada uvāca
na manas tṛptim ādhatte kathāḥ śṛṇvat tvayeritāḥ
pṛthak tīrthaphalaṃ śrotuṃ pravṛttaṃ mama mānasam //
79.d:
नारद उवाच
न मनस् तृप्तिम् आधत्ते कथाः शृण्वत् त्वयेरिताः
पृथक् तीर्थफलं श्रोतुं प्रवृत्तं मम मानसम् ॥
79.m: Nārada said: / My mind finds no satiety in hearing the stories told by you. / My mind has set out to hear the specific fruits of the holy places.

79.s:
kramaśo brāhmaṇānītāṃ gaṅgāṃ me prathamaṃ vada
pṛthak tīrthaphalaṃ puṇyaṃ setihāsaṃ yathākramam //
79.d:
क्रमशो ब्राह्मणानीतां गङ्गां मे प्रथमं वद
पृथक् तीर्थफलं पुण्यं सेतिहासं यथाक्रमम् ॥
79.m: Tell me first in order of the Gaṅgā brought by the brāhmaṇa, / the holy, specific fruit of the holy place in order, along with its history.

79.s:
brahmovāca
tīrthānāṃ ca pṛthag bhāvaṃ phalaṃ māhātmyam eva ca
sarvaṃ vaktuṃ na śaknomi na ca tvaṃ śravaṇe kṣamaḥ //
79.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तीर्थानां च पृथग् भावं फलं माहात्म्यम् एव च
सर्वं वक्तुं न शक्नोमि न च त्वं श्रवणे क्षमः ॥
79.m: Brahmā said: / The distinct existence of the holy places, their fruit, and their majesty— / I am not able to tell all of it, nor are you capable of hearing it.

79.s:
tathāpi kiṃcid vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada yatnataḥ
yāny uktāni ca tīrthāni śrutivākyāni yāni ca //
79.d:
तथापि किंचिद् वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद यत्नतः
यान्य् उक्तानि च तीर्थानि श्रुतिवाक्यानि यानि च ॥
79.m: Nevertheless, I shall tell a little; listen attentively, O Nārada, / to the holy places that have been spoken of and to the statements of the scriptures.

79.s:
tāni vakṣyāmi saṃkṣepān namaskṛtvā trilocanam
yatrāsau bhagavān āsīt pratyakṣas tryambako mune //
79.d:
तानि वक्ष्यामि संक्षेपान् नमस्कृत्वा त्रिलोचनम्
यत्रासौ भगवान् आसीत् प्रत्यक्षस् त्र्यम्बको मुने ॥
79.m: I will tell them in brief, having bowed to the Three-eyed Lord, / where that Lord Tryambaka was visibly present, O sage.

79.s:
tryambakaṃ nāma tat tīrthaṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam
vārāham aparaṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam //
79.d:
त्र्यम्बकं नाम तत् तीर्थं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम्
वाराहम् अपरं तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥
79.m: Tryambaka is the name of that holy place, which bestows enjoyment and liberation. / Another holy place is Vārāha, renowned throughout the three worlds.

79.s:
tasya rūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi nāma viṣṇor yathābhavat
purā devān parābhūya yajñam ādāya rākṣasaḥ //
79.d:
तस्य रूपं प्रवक्ष्यामि नाम विष्णोर् यथाभवत्
पुरा देवान् पराभूय यज्ञम् आदाय राक्षसः ॥
79.m: I will tell of its nature, and how the name of Viṣṇu came to be. / Formerly, a rākṣasa, having vanquished the gods and seized the sacrifice,

79.s:
rasātalam anuprāptaḥ sindhusena iti śrutaḥ
yajñe talam anuprāpte niryajñā hy abhavan mahī //
79.d:
रसातलम् अनुप्राप्तः सिन्धुसेन इति श्रुतः
यज्ञे तलम् अनुप्राप्ते निर्यज्ञा ह्य् अभवन् मही ॥
79.m: reached Rasātala; he was known as Sindhusena. / When the sacrifice had reached the netherworld, the earth indeed became devoid of sacrifice.

79.s:
nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro yajñe naṣṭa itītvarāḥ
surās tam eva viviśū rasātalam anudviṣam //
79.d:
नायं लोको ऽस्ति न परो यज्ञे नष्ट इतीत्वराः
सुरास् तम् एव विविशू रसातलम् अनुद्विषम् ॥
79.m: "When sacrifice is destroyed, there is neither this world nor the next." So saying, wandering, / the gods entered that very Rasātala, pursuing the enemy.

79.s:
nāśaknuvaṃs tu taṃ jetuṃ devā indrapurogamāḥ
viṣṇuṃ purāṇapuruṣaṃ gatvā tasmai nyavedayan //
79.d:
नाशक्नुवंस् तु तं जेतुं देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः
विष्णुं पुराणपुरुषं गत्वा तस्मै न्यवेदयन् ॥
79.m: The gods, led by Indra, were not able to defeat him. / Approaching Viṣṇu, the primordial Person, they reported to him

79.s:
rākṣasasya tu tat karma yajñabhraṃśam aśeṣataḥ
tataḥ provāca bhagavān vārāhaṃ vapur āsthitaḥ //
79.d:
राक्षसस्य तु तत् कर्म यज्ञभ्रंशम् अशेषतः
ततः प्रोवाच भगवान् वाराहं वपुर् आस्थितः ॥
79.m: that deed of the rākṣasa, the complete loss of the sacrifice. / Thereupon the Lord, assuming the form of the Boar,

79.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇir gatvā caiva rasātalam
ānayiṣye makhaṃ puṇyaṃ hatvā rākṣasapuṃgavān //
79.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिर् गत्वा चैव रसातलम्
आनयिष्ये मखं पुण्यं हत्वा राक्षसपुंगवान् ॥
79.m: with conch, discus, and mace in hand, [said:] "Going to Rasātala, / I will bring back the holy sacrifice, having slain the foremost rākṣasas.

79.s:
svaḥ prayāntu surāḥ sarve vyetu vo mānaso jvaraḥ
yena gaṅgā talaṃ prāptā pathā tenaiva cakradhṛk //
79.d:
स्वः प्रयान्तु सुराः सर्वे व्येतु वो मानसो ज्वरः
येन गङ्गा तलं प्राप्ता पथा तेनैव चक्रधृक् ॥
79.m: Let all the gods go to heaven; let the fever of your minds depart." / By the very path by which the Gaṅgā reached the netherworld, the wielder of the discus

79.s:
jagāma tarasā putra bhuvaṃ bhittvā rasātalam
sa varāhavapuḥ śrīmān rasātalanivāsinaḥ //
79.d:
जगाम तरसा पुत्र भुवं भित्त्वा रसातलम्
स वराहवपुः श्रीमान् रसातलनिवासिनः ॥
79.m: went swiftly, O son, cleaving the earth to Rasātala. / That glorious one in the form of a boar [slew] the dwellers of Rasātala;

79.s:
rākṣasān dānavān hatvā mukhe dhṛtvā mahādhvaram
vārāharūpī bhagavān makham ādāya yajñabhuk //
79.d:
राक्षसान् दानवान् हत्वा मुखे धृत्वा महाध्वरम्
वाराहरूपी भगवान् मखम् आदाय यज्ञभुक् ॥
79.m: having slain the rākṣasas and dānavas, holding the great sacrifice in his mouth, / the Lord in the form of the Boar, the enjoyer of sacrifice, took the sacrifice.

79.s:
yena prāpa talaṃ viṣṇuḥ pathā tenaiva śatrujit
mukhe nyasya mahāyajñaṃ niścakrāma rasātalāt //
79.d:
येन प्राप तलं विष्णुः पथा तेनैव शत्रुजित्
मुखे न्यस्य महायज्ञं निश्चक्राम रसातलात् ॥
79.m: By the very path by which Viṣṇu reached the netherworld, the conqueror of enemies / emerged from Rasātala, placing the great sacrifice in his mouth.

79.s:
tatra brahmagirau devāḥ pratīkṣāṃ cakrire hareḥ
pathas tasmād viniḥsṛtya gaṅgāsravaṇam abhyagāt //
79.d:
तत्र ब्रह्मगिरौ देवाः प्रतीक्षां चक्रिरे हरेः
पथस् तस्माद् विनिःसृत्य गङ्गास्रवणम् अभ्यगात् ॥
79.m: There on the Brahmagiri the gods waited for Hari. / Emerging from that path, he approached the fountain of the Gaṅgā,

79.s:
prākṣālayac ca svāṅgāni asṛgliptāni nārada
gaṅgāmbhasā tatra kuṇḍaṃ vārāham abhavat tataḥ //
79.d:
प्राक्षालयच् च स्वाङ्गानि असृग्लिप्तानि नारद
गङ्गाम्भसा तत्र कुण्डं वाराहम् अभवत् ततः ॥
79.m: and washed his limbs that were smeared with blood, O Nārada, / with the water of the Gaṅgā. Thereupon arose the Vārāha pool.

79.s:
mukhe nyastaṃ mahāyajñaṃ devānāṃ purato hariḥ
dattavāṃs tridaśaśreṣṭho mukhād yajño 'bhyajāyata //
79.d:
मुखे न्यस्तं महायज्ञं देवानां पुरतो हरिः
दत्तवांस् त्रिदशश्रेष्ठो मुखाद् यज्ञो ऽभ्यजायत ॥
79.m: The great sacrifice held in his mouth, Hari, best of the thirty gods, / gave before the gods; from his mouth the sacrifice was reborn.

79.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti yajñāṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ sruva ucyate
vārāharūpam abhavad evaṃ vai kāraṇāntarāt //
79.d:
ततः प्रभृति यज्ञाङ्गं प्रधानं स्रुव उच्यते
वाराहरूपम् अभवद् एवं वै कारणान्तरात् ॥
79.m: From that time forward, the ladle is called the principal part of the sacrifice. / Thus indeed he took the form of the Boar on account of a different reason.

79.s:
tasmāt puṇyatamaṃ tīrthaṃ vārāhaṃ sarvakāmadam
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sarvakratuphalapradam //
79.d:
तस्मात् पुण्यतमं तीर्थं वाराहं सर्वकामदम्
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम् ॥
79.m: Therefore the Vārāha holy place is most sacred and grants all desires; / bathing and giving gifts there bestows the fruit of all sacrifices.

79.s:
tatra sthito 'pi yaḥ kaścit pitṝn smarati puṇyakṛt
vimuktāḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ pitaraḥ svargam āpnuyuḥ //
79.d:
तत्र स्थितो ऽपि यः कश्चित् पितॄन् स्मरति पुण्यकृत्
विमुक्ताः सर्वपापेभ्यः पितरः स्वर्गम् आप्नुयुः ॥
79.m: Even when staying there, whatever doer of holy deeds remembers his ancestors, / his ancestors, freed from all sins, will attain heaven.

80.s:
brahmovāca
kuśāvartasya māhātmyam ahaṃ vaktuṃ na te kṣamaḥ
tasya smaraṇamātreṇa kṛtakṛtyo bhaven naraḥ //
80.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कुशावर्तस्य माहात्म्यम् अहं वक्तुं न ते क्षमः
तस्य स्मरणमात्रेण कृतकृत्यो भवेन् नरः ॥
80.m: Brahmā said: / I am not able to tell you the greatness of Kuśāvarta; / by the mere remembrance of it a person becomes one who has accomplished his purpose.

80.s:
kuśāvartam iti khyātaṃ narāṇāṃ sarvakāmadam
kuśenāvartitaṃ yatra gautamena mahātmanā //
80.d:
कुशावर्तम् इति ख्यातं नराणां सर्वकामदम्
कुशेनावर्तितं यत्र गौतमेन महात्मना ॥
80.m: Famous as Kuśāvarta, it grants all desires to human beings, / where she was turned around with a kuśa blade by the great-souled Gautama.

80.s:
kuśenāvartayitvā tu ānayām āsa tāṃ muniḥ
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ tṛptidāyakam //
80.d:
कुशेनावर्तयित्वा तु आनयाम् आस तां मुनिः
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च पितॄणां तृप्तिदायकम् ॥
80.m: Having turned her around with a kuśa blade, the sage brought her down; / bathing and giving gifts there brings satisfaction to the ancestors.

80.s:
nīlagaṅgā saricchreṣṭhā niḥsṛtā nīlaparvatāt
tatra snānādi yat kiṃcit karoti prayato naraḥ //
80.d:
नीलगङ्गा सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा निःसृता नीलपर्वतात्
तत्र स्नानादि यत् किंचित् करोति प्रयतो नरः ॥
80.m: The Nīlagaṅgā, best of rivers, issued forth from the Nīla mountain; / whatever bathing and the like a restrained person performs there,

80.s:
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ vidyāt pitṝṇāṃ tṛptidāyakam
viśrutaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kapotaṃ tīrtham uttamam //
80.d:
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं विद्यात् पितॄणां तृप्तिदायकम्
विश्रुतं त्रिषु लोकेषु कपोतं तीर्थम् उत्तमम् ॥
80.m: he should know that all of it is imperishable and brings satisfaction to the ancestors. / Renowned in the three worlds is the excellent holy place Kapota.

80.s:
tasya rūpaṃ ca vakṣyāmi mune śṛṇu mahāphalam
tatra brahmagirau kaścid vyādhaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ //
80.d:
तस्य रूपं च वक्ष्यामि मुने शृणु महाफलम्
तत्र ब्रह्मगिरौ कश्चिद् व्याधः परमदारुणः ॥
80.m: I will tell of its nature and its great fruit; listen, O sage: / there on the Brahmagiri lived a certain extremely cruel hunter,

80.s:
hinasti brāhmaṇān sādhūn yatīn gopakṣiṇo mṛgān
evaṃbhūtaḥ sa pāpātmā krodhano 'nṛtabhāṣaṇaḥ //
80.d:
हिनस्ति ब्राह्मणान् साधून् यतीन् गोपक्षिणो मृगान्
एवंभूतः स पापात्मा क्रोधनो ऽनृतभाषणः ॥
80.m: who harmed brāhmaṇas, virtuous men, ascetics, cows, birds, and deer. / Such was he, an evil-minded, wrathful speaker of untruth,

80.s:
bhīṣaṇākṛtir atyugro nīlākṣo hrasvabāhukaḥ
danturo naṣṭanāsākṣo hrasvapāt pṛthukukṣikaḥ //
80.d:
भीषणाकृतिर् अत्युग्रो नीलाक्षो ह्रस्वबाहुकः
दन्तुरो नष्टनासाक्षो ह्रस्वपात् पृथुकुक्षिकः ॥
80.m: of terrifying form, exceedingly fierce, blue-eyed, short-armed, / buck-toothed, with ruined nose and eyes, short-legged, broad-bellied,

80.s:
hrasvodaro hrasvabhujo vikṛto gardabhasvanaḥ
pāśahastaḥ pāpacittaḥ pāpiṣṭhaḥ sadhanuḥ sadā //
80.d:
ह्रस्वोदरो ह्रस्वभुजो विकृतो गर्दभस्वनः
पाशहस्तः पापचित्तः पापिष्ठः सधनुः सदा ॥
80.m: short-waisted, short-armed, deformed, with the bray of a donkey, / noose in hand, evil-minded, most wicked, always carrying a bow.

80.s:
tasya bhāryā tathābhūtā apatyāny api nārada
tayā tu preryamāṇo 'sau viveśa gahanaṃ vanam //
80.d:
तस्य भार्या तथाभूता अपत्यान्य् अपि नारद
तया तु प्रेर्यमाणो ऽसौ विवेश गहनं वनम् ॥
80.m: His wife was like him, and his children too, O Nārada; / urged on by her, he entered the dense forest.

80.s:
sa jaghāna mṛgān pāpaḥ pakṣiṇo bahurūpiṇaḥ
pañjare prākṣipat kāṃścij jīvamānāṃs tathetarān //
80.d:
स जघान मृगान् पापः पक्षिणो बहुरूपिणः
पञ्जरे प्राक्षिपत् कांश्चिज् जीवमानांस् तथेतरान् ॥
80.m: The wicked man killed deer and birds of various kinds; / some he cast into a cage while still alive, and others likewise.

80.s:
kṣudhayā paritaptāṅgo vihvalas tṛṣayā tathā
bhrāntadeśo bahutaraṃ nyavartata gṛhaṃ prati //
80.d:
क्षुधया परितप्ताङ्गो विह्वलस् तृषया तथा
भ्रान्तदेशो बहुतरं न्यवर्तत गृहं प्रति ॥
80.m: With limbs tormented by hunger, and bewildered by thirst, / having wandered across vast country, he turned back toward home.

80.s:
tato 'parāhṇe saṃprāpte nivṛtte madhumādhave
kṣaṇāt taḍid garjitaṃ ca sābhraṃ caivābhavat tadā //
80.d:
ततो ऽपराह्णे संप्राप्ते निवृत्ते मधुमाधवे
क्षणात् तडिद् गर्जितं च साभ्रं चैवाभवत् तदा ॥
80.m: Then, as afternoon arrived and the spring months were past, / in an instant lightning and thunder and clouds arose.

80.s:
vavau vāyuḥ sāśmavarṣo vāridhārātibhīṣaṇaḥ
sa gacchaṃl lubdhakaḥ śrāntaḥ panthānaṃ nāvabudhyata //
80.d:
ववौ वायुः साश्मवर्षो वारिधारातिभीषणः
स गच्छंल् लुब्धकः श्रान्तः पन्थानं नावबुध्यत ॥
80.m: A wind blew with a shower of stones, terrifying with torrential streams of water; / walking along, exhausted, the hunter could not see the path.

80.s:
jalaṃ sthalaṃ gartam atho panthānam athavā diśaḥ
na bubodha tadā pāpaḥ śrāntaḥ śaraṇam apy atha //
80.d:
जलं स्थलं गर्तम् अथो पन्थानम् अथवा दिशः
न बुबोध तदा पापः श्रान्तः शरणम् अप्य् अथ ॥
80.m: Water, dry land, a pit, or the path, or the directions— / the wicked man, exhausted, could not distinguish then, nor any shelter.

80.s:
kva gacchāmi kva tiṣṭheyaṃ kiṃ karomīty acintayat
sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇān āhartāhaṃ yathāntakaḥ //
80.d:
क्व गच्छामि क्व तिष्ठेयं किं करोमीत्य् अचिन्तयत्
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां प्राणान् आहर्ताहं यथान्तकः ॥
80.m: "Where do I go? Where should I stay? What do I do?" he thought; / "I am the taker of the lives of all living beings, like Antaka;

80.s:
mamāpy antakaraṃ bhūtaṃ saṃprāptaṃ cāśmavarṣaṇam
trātāraṃ naiva paśyāmi śilāṃ vā vṛkṣam antike //
80.d:
ममाप्य् अन्तकरं भूतं संप्राप्तं चाश्मवर्षणम्
त्रातारं नैव पश्यामि शिलां वा वृक्षम् अन्तिके ॥
80.m: and now the bringer of my own end has arrived, a shower of stones; / I see no protector, nor a rock or tree nearby."

80.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vyādho vicintyāpaśyad antike
vane vanaspatim iva nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathātrijam //
80.d:
एवं बहुविधं व्याधो विचिन्त्यापश्यद् अन्तिके
वने वनस्पतिम् इव नक्षत्राणां यथात्रिजम् ॥
80.m: Having pondered in many ways like this, the hunter saw nearby / a lord of the forest in the woods, like the moon among the constellations,

80.s:
mṛgāṇāṃ ca yathā siṃham āśramāṇāṃ gṛhādhipam
indriyāṇāṃ mana iva trātāraṃ prāṇināṃ nagam //
80.d:
मृगाणां च यथा सिंहम् आश्रमाणां गृहाधिपम्
इन्द्रियाणां मन इव त्रातारं प्राणिनां नगम् ॥
80.m: like a lion among beasts, a householder among the stages of life, / like the mind among the sense organs—a tree that was a protector for living beings,

80.s:
śreṣṭhaṃ viṭapinaṃ śubhraṃ śākhāpallavamaṇḍitam
tam āśrityopaviṣṭo 'bhūt klinnavāsā sa lubdhakaḥ //
80.d:
श्रेष्ठं विटपिनं शुभ्रं शाखापल्लवमण्डितम्
तम् आश्रित्योपविष्टो ऽभूत् क्लिन्नवासा स लुब्धकः ॥
80.m: a splendid tree, bright, adorned with branches and sprouts. / Resorting to it, the hunter sat down, his clothes soaked.

80.s:
smaran bhāryām apatyāni jīveyur athavā na vā
etasminn antare tatra cāstaṃ prāpto divākaraḥ //
80.d:
स्मरन् भार्याम् अपत्यानि जीवेयुर् अथवा न वा
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र चास्तं प्राप्तो दिवाकरः ॥
80.m: Thinking of his wife and children—whether they would live or not— / in the meantime, the sun set.

80.s:
tam eva nagam āśritya kapoto bhāryayā saha
putrapautraiḥ parivṛto hy āste tatra nagottame //
80.d:
तम् एव नगम् आश्रित्य कपोतो भार्यया सह
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतो ह्य् आस्ते तत्र नगोत्तमे ॥
80.m: Resorting to that very tree, a pigeon with his wife / lived there on that best of trees, surrounded by sons and grandsons.

80.s:
sukhena nirbhayo bhūtvā sutṛptaḥ prīta eva ca
bahavo vatsarā yātā vasatas tasya pakṣiṇaḥ //
80.d:
सुखेन निर्भयो भूत्वा सुतृप्तः प्रीत एव च
बहवो वत्सरा याता वसतस् तस्य पक्षिणः ॥
80.m: Living happily, free of fear, well-satisfied, and delighted, / many years had passed for that dwelling bird.

80.s:
pativratā tasya bhāryā suprītā tena caiva hi
koṭare tannage śreṣṭhe jalavāyvagnivarjite //
80.d:
पतिव्रता तस्य भार्या सुप्रीता तेन चैव हि
कोटरे तन्नगे श्रेष्ठे जलवाय्वग्निवर्जिते ॥
80.m: His wife was devoted to her husband, and she was well-pleased with him; / in a hollow in that best of trees, free from water, wind, and fire,

80.s:
bhāryāputraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvadāste kapotakaḥ
tasmin dine daivavaśāt kapotaś ca kapotakī //
80.d:
भार्यापुत्रैः परिवृतः सर्वदास्ते कपोतकः
तस्मिन् दिने दैववशात् कपोतश् च कपोतकी ॥
80.m: surrounded by wife and sons, the pigeon lived always. / On that day, by the force of fate, the pigeon and his female mate

80.s:
bhakṣyārthaṃ tu ubhau yātau kapoto nagam abhyagāt
sāpi daivavaśāt putra pañjarasthaiva vartate //
80.d:
भक्ष्यार्थं तु उभौ यातौ कपोतो नगम् अभ्यगात्
सापि दैववशात् पुत्र पञ्जरस्थैव वर्तते ॥
80.m: both went out for food; the pigeon returned to the tree, / but she, by the force of fate, O son, was sitting in a cage.

80.s:
gṛhītā lubdhakenātha jīvamāneva vartate
kapotako 'py apatyāni mātṛhīnāny udīkṣya ca //
80.d:
गृहीता लुब्धकेनाथ जीवमानेव वर्तते
कपोतको ऽप्य् अपत्यानि मातृहीनान्य् उदीक्ष्य च ॥
80.m: Seized by the hunter, she was kept alive; / and the pigeon, seeing his children bereft of their mother,

80.s:
varṣaṃ ca bhīṣaṇaṃ prāptam astaṃ yāto divākaraḥ
svakoṭaraṃ tayā hīnam ālokya vilalāpa saḥ //
80.d:
वर्षं च भीषणं प्राप्तम् अस्तं यातो दिवाकरः
स्वकोटरं तया हीनम् आलोक्य विललाप सः ॥
80.m: and seeing the terrifying rain arrive and the sun set, / beholding his hollow empty of her, he lamented:

80.s:
tāṃ baddhāṃ pañjarasthāṃ vā na bubodha kapotarāṭ
anvārebhe kapoto vai priyāyā guṇakīrtanam //
80.d:
तां बद्धां पञ्जरस्थां वा न बुबोध कपोतराट्
अन्वारेभे कपोतो वै प्रियाया गुणकीर्तनम् ॥
80.m: The king of pigeons did not know that she was bound or inside a cage; / the pigeon indeed began to recount the virtues of his beloved:

80.s:
nādyāpy āyāti kalyāṇī mama harṣavivardhinī
mama dharmasya jananī mama dehasya ceśvarī //
80.d:
नाद्याप्य् आयाति कल्याणी मम हर्षविवर्धिनी
मम धर्मस्य जननी मम देहस्य चेश्वरी ॥
80.m: "Even now the auspicious one does not come, she who increases my joy, / the mother of my dharma, and the mistress of my body.

80.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ saiva nityaṃ sahāyinī
tuṣṭe hasantī ruṣṭe ca mama duḥkhapramārjanī //
80.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां सैव नित्यं सहायिनी
तुष्टे हसन्ती रुष्टे च मम दुःखप्रमार्जनी ॥
80.m: She is always my companion in dharma, worldly gain, pleasure, and liberation; / laughing when I am pleased, and wiper of my sorrow when I am angry.

80.s:
sakhī mantreṣu sā nityaṃ mama vākyaratā sadā
nādyāpy āyāti kalyāṇī saṃprayāte 'pi bhāskare //
80.d:
सखी मन्त्रेषु सा नित्यं मम वाक्यरता सदा
नाद्याप्य् आयाति कल्याणी संप्रयाते ऽपि भास्करे ॥
80.m: A constant friend in consultations, she is always devoted to my words; / even now the auspicious one does not come, though the sun has set.

80.s:
na jānāti vrataṃ mantraṃ daivaṃ dharmārtham eva ca
pativratā patiprāṇā patimantrā patipriyā //
80.d:
न जानाति व्रतं मन्त्रं दैवं धर्मार्थम् एव च
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा पतिमन्त्रा पतिप्रिया ॥
80.m: She knows no vow, sacred formula, deity, or dharma and wealth [apart from me]; / devoted to her husband, holding her husband as her life, whose sacred formula is her husband, dear to her husband.

80.s:
nādyāpy āyāti kalyāṇī kiṃ karomi kva yāmi vā
kiṃ me gṛhaṃ kānanaṃ ca tayā hīnaṃ hi dṛśyate //
80.d:
नाद्याप्य् आयाति कल्याणी किं करोमि क्व यामि वा
किं मे गृहं काननं च तया हीनं हि दृश्यते ॥
80.m: Even now the auspicious one does not come; what shall I do, or where shall I go? / Why does my house and forest appear deserted without her?

80.s:
tayā yuktaṃ śriyā yuktaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ vāpi śobhanam
nādyāpy āyāti me kāntā yayā gṛham udīritam //
80.d:
तया युक्तं श्रिया युक्तं भीषणं वापि शोभनम्
नाद्याप्य् आयाति मे कान्ता यया गृहम् उदीरितम् ॥
80.m: Accompanied by her, it was endowed with splendour, whether terrifying or beautiful; / even now my beloved does not come, by whom home was defined.

80.s:
vinānayā na jīviṣye tyaje vāpi priyāṃ tanum
kiṃ kurvantu tv apatyāni luptadharmas tv ahaṃ punaḥ //
80.d:
विनानया न जीविष्ये त्यजे वापि प्रियां तनुम्
किं कुर्वन्तु त्व् अपत्यानि लुप्तधर्मस् त्व् अहं पुनः ॥
80.m: Without her I will not live, or I will abandon my dear body; / but what will my children do, since I have fallen away from dharma?"

80.s:
evaṃ vilapatas tasya bhartur vākyaṃ niśamya sā
pañjarasthaiva sā vākyaṃ bhartāram idam abravīt //
80.d:
एवं विलपतस् तस्य भर्तुर् वाक्यं निशम्य सा
पञ्जरस्थैव सा वाक्यं भर्तारम् इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥
80.m: Hearing this speech of her husband as he was lamenting in this way, / she, while still in the cage, spoke this word to her husband:

80.s:
kapotaky uvāca
atrāham asmi baddhaiva vivaśāsmi khagottama
ānītāhaṃ lubdhakena baddhā pāśair mahāmate //
80.d:
कपोतक्य् उवाच
अत्राहम् अस्मि बद्धैव विवशास्मि खगोत्तम
आनीताहं लुब्धकेन बद्धा पाशैर् महामते ॥
80.m: The female pigeon said: / "Here I am, captive indeed, helpless, O best of birds; / I was brought by the hunter, bound with snares, O noble-minded one.

80.s:
dhanyāsmy anugṛhītāsmi patir vakti guṇān mama
sato vāpy asato vāpi kṛtārthāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
80.d:
धन्यास्म्य् अनुगृहीतास्मि पतिर् वक्ति गुणान् मम
सतो वाप्य् असतो वापि कृतार्थाहं न संशयः ॥
80.m: I am fortunate, I am favoured, that my husband speaks of my virtues; / whether true or untrue, I have attained my purpose, there is no doubt.

80.s:
tuṣṭe bhartari nārīṇāṃ tuṣṭāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ
viparyaye tu nārīṇām avaśyaṃ nāśam āpnuyāt //
80.d:
तुष्टे भर्तरि नारीणां तुष्टाः स्युः सर्वदेवताः
विपर्यये तु नारीणाम् अवश्यं नाशम् आप्नुयात् ॥
80.m: When a husband is pleased, all the gods are pleased with women; / but in the opposite case, women surely meet with ruin.

80.s:
tvaṃ daivaṃ tvaṃ prabhur mahyaṃ tvaṃ suhṛt tvaṃ parāyaṇam
tvaṃ vrataṃ tvaṃ paraṃ brahma svargo mokṣas tvam eva ca //
80.d:
त्वं दैवं त्वं प्रभुर् मह्यं त्वं सुहृत् त्वं परायणम्
त्वं व्रतं त्वं परं ब्रह्म स्वर्गो मोक्षस् त्वम् एव च ॥
80.m: You are my deity, you are my lord, you are my friend, you are my supreme refuge; / you are my vow, you are supreme brahman, you are heaven and liberation itself.

80.s:
mā cintāṃ kuru kalyāṇa dharme buddhiṃ sthirāṃ kuru
tvatprasādāc ca bhuktā hi bhogāś ca vividhā mayā
alaṃ khedena majjena dharme buddhiṃ kuru sthirām //
80.d:
मा चिन्तां कुरु कल्याण धर्मे बुद्धिं स्थिरां कुरु
त्वत्प्रसादाच् च भुक्ता हि भोगाश् च विविधा मया
अलं खेदेन मज्जेन धर्मे बुद्धिं कुरु स्थिराम् ॥
80.m: Do not worry, O auspicious one; fix your mind firmly on dharma. / Through your favour, various pleasures have indeed been enjoyed by me; / enough of grief, O dear one; fix your mind firmly on dharma."
